News.title: Addiction centre intern ‘had sex with patient in therapy sessions & took him to mum’s home to romp’ as she faces jail
News.content:
TWISTED ROMANCE Addiction centre intern ‘had sex with patient in therapy sessions & took him to mum’s home to romp’ as she faces jail

AN ADDICTION centre intern has been accused of having sex with a patient during therapy and taking him to his mum’s home to romp.

Michelle Luchau-Rebora, 32, has been charged with sexual misconduct by a psychotherapist and now faces five years in jail.



She appeared in court on Wednesday wearing a green anti-suicide smock.

The accused turned herself in after the patient, an unnamed 42-year-old man, reported her.



Shortly before, she had called off their alleged three-month intimate relationship, according to court documents.

Luchau-Rebora allegedly started the romance in June 2025 while working as an intern at the New Hope C.O.R.P.S. addiction treatment center in Homestead, Florida.

The pair allegedly had sex during therapy sessions.

Luchau-Rebora also “facilitated alibis on his behalf, which allowed him authorization to leave the restricted facility and engage in sexual intercourse on multiple occasions”, according to court documents.



They allegedly had sex at her home in Pinecrest, the suspect‘s mother’s property in Key Biscayne, and in the Miami Jackson Memorial Hospital.

The intern demanded that he not tell anyone about their relationship because it would “affect her ability to work as a therapist”, the documents claimed.

Luchau-Rebora ended the alleged relationship last autumn.

The man then reported her to facility officials, who then contacted police, the documents state.

Stephen Alvarez, the New Hope C.O.R.P.S. executive director, told WPLG: “Upon becoming aware of the allegations, New Hope promptly reported the matter to the appropriate authorities and agencies, terminated the individual’s internship, and fully cooperated with the subsequent investigation.”



The former intern has since been charged with sexual misconduct by a psychotherapist – a third-degree felony in Florida.

She faces five years behind bars if convicted.

Luchau-Rebora is no longer in custody after posting a $5,000 bond Wednesday night.

“I’m not going to comment on anything. You can ask my lawyer,” she told a Florida journalist before telling them to leave her alone.

“This is kinda weird,” she added. “I really don’t wanna add anything right now.”

News.title: Two women ‘sexually assaulted’ at pub in UK industrial town – as CCTV released
News.content:
PUB HORROR Two women ‘sexually assaulted’ at pub in UK industrial town – as CCTV released

COPS have released CCTV images of a man after two women were reportedly sexually assaulted at a pub.

The force says the man “inappropriately touched” both victims during the incident in the early hours of Sunday, July 19.

The pair were reportedly approached by him at the New Imperial on Albert Road, Widnes, near Cheshire.

It happened sometime between 12.03am and 12.15am, with officers launching an investigation following the reports.





Now cops have released CCTV images of a man they believe could assist with their enquiries.

Police Constable Jade Bellerby said: “Our enquiries into this incident are ongoing, and we are urging anyone who recognises the man pictured to get in touch.

“We believe he may be from the South Wales area and would also appeal directly to him to contact us.

“We would also like to hear from anyone with dashcam or CCTV footage that could assist our investigation, or from anyone who witnessed the incident.”

Anyone with information is urged to contact police, quoting reference IML-2376862.

News.title: Moment kidnap victim jumps into tree from first-floor window & flags down cops… before gang arrested at gunpoint
News.content:
THIS is the moment a kidnap victim leaps from a first-floor window into a tree in a desperate bid to escape his captors before armed cops swoop on the gang and arrest them.

The victim was lured to an address in Market Rasen, Lincolnshire, on July 4 last year where he was held against his will.



At the property he was subjected to abuse and humiliation over the course of a day by Brad’Lee Ranyard, Nathan Gladwell, Jackson Nicholson, Craig Ranyard and Danielle Thompson.

Following the harrowing ordeal, which the thugs filmed on their phones, the victim was forced into the back of a pickup truck.



He was then driven to another property in Lincoln where he was again held against his will.

Video footage released by police shows him mounting a desperate escape from the property on Portland Street.

The victim can be seen clambering from a first floor window onto a balcony before taking his chance and leaping into the branches of a nearby tree.

A window in the flat opens and a man peers out before the victim then falls to the ground and runs off down the street just as a police car drives up the road towards him.



The terrified kidnap victim jumps into the road in front of the police car before climbing into the back of the vehicle and telling the officers he needs help.

He was brought to safety by the cops, who then took an account of his ordeal.

Following the daring escape, two of the suspects were seen leaving the flat before returning with a duffle bag.

They then leave the property again and get into a pickup truck parked nearby.

The pickup was tracked before eventually being stopped by armed police who arrested the two suspects.



Gun cops leap from their vehicle when the pickup pulls over and aim their rifles at the two suspects, who hold their hands up.

The pair are ordered to stand still and keep their hands up before they are cuffed by the responding cops.

Three other suspects were arrested later the same evening at an address in Market Rasen.



On Friday 28 August, all five appeared at Lincoln Crown Court to be sentenced for their roles in the kidnap.

The court heard that the victim had been subjected to the harrowing ordeal following the breakdown of a past relationship.

Brad’Lee Ranyard, 20, of Portland Street, Lincoln, was jailed for nine years after being convicted of kidnap and pleading guilty to false imprisonment.

Jackson Nicholson, 25, of Lindsay Drive, Gainsborough, was also jailed for nine years after being convicted of kidnap and pleading guilty to false imprisonment.

Craig Ranyard, 42, of Barsey Walk, Horncastle, was sentenced to five years and three months’ imprisonment after being convicted of false imprisonment.



Danielle Thompson, 38, of Lime Walk, Market Rasen, was sentenced to four years and nine months’ imprisonment after being convicted of false imprisonment.

Nathan Gladwell, 36, of Union Street, Market Rasen, was sentenced to three years and seven months’ imprisonment after being convicted of false imprisonment.

The five thugs were also handed an indefinite restraining order preventing them from contacting the victim or members of his family.

DC Liam Henderson, who led the investigation, said: “This was a sustained and deeply distressing ordeal in which a man was subjected to violence, threats and humiliation at the hands of people who appeared to find amusement in his suffering.

“The victim showed remarkable courage in seizing the opportunity to escape.



“The CCTV footage captures a desperate moment in which he quite literally risked everything to get away from those holding him captive.

“By sheer chance, as he fled from the property, a marked police vehicle entered the street.

“That moment changed the course of events and allowed officers to get him to safety when he needed help most.

“We often hear concerns that victims may feel alone or that help will not arrive when it is needed.

“This case is a powerful reminder that when someone reaches out for help, we will do everything we can to protect them and bring those responsible to justice.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The impact on the victim has been significant, and our thoughts remain with him as he continues to recover from this traumatic experience.

“I would also like to commend the officers involved, whose actions that day ensured a vulnerable man was brought to safety and that those responsible were swiftly arrested and brought before the courts.”

News.title: How missing capybara is STILL on the run five months after escaping from UK zoo as hope renewed with latest sighting
News.content:
A MISSING capybara still on the run five months after escaping from a UK zoo has finally being spotted for the first time since March.

Samba vanished from Marwell Zoo in Hampshire on March 17 while she and her sister Tango were being moved into a temporary enclosure.



Now, a photograph taken by a member of the public has confirmed the fugitive rodent is still alive.

The picture was sent to Marwell after the reported sighting and has since been verified by the zoo as Samba.



A Marwell spokesman said: “Yes, the sighting was Samba, but we haven’t got any further updates to share at the moment.”

The sighting has renewed hopes of finally bringing the nine-month-old capybara home after months of mystery surrounding her whereabouts.



Samba disappeared after escaping from her enclosure, while sister Tango was found nearby and safely returned.

But Samba proved far more elusive, despite a huge search operation involving drones, dog units, camera traps and volunteers.



Her disappearance sparked widespread interest, with members of the public reporting possible sightings as the search continued.

Back in March, Samba was reportedly spotted sunning herself on riverbanks after apparently travelling more than a mile from the zoo.

She was thought to have crossed a busy road, avoided electric fences and even dodged herds of cows.

At one point she was seen near The Ship Inn in Owslebury before diving into undergrowth.

She later resurfaced on the banks of the River Itchen, around two-and-a-half miles away, before another sighting near Twyford.



Zoo staff warned at the time that the biggest dangers facing Samba were people and roads.

Capybaras are native to South America and are the world’s biggest rodents, growing to more than 5ft and weighing up to 12st.

They are also well suited to life around water and have no natural predators in the UK.



The zoo has previously said Samba had access to fresh water, vegetation and places to shelter while out in the wild.

On August 11, Marwell said its teams were acting on a “promising lead” following a reported sighting.

The latest photograph has now provided the clearest proof yet that Samba has managed to survive her extraordinary five-month adventure.

Her disappearance has also inspired a string of jokes online, with social media users sharing pictures of the capybara apparently living her best life.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Some have even posted AI-generated images showing Samba lounging by pools, relaxing on holiday or enjoying a trip to the pub.



But despite the jokes, the zoo’s search for the runaway rodent is still ongoing.

News.title: Paddy Power faces shutting 100 shops with the loss of 400 jobs due to Labour’s tax hikes on betting
News.content:
PADDY Power bosses face closing up to 100 stores with the loss of four hundred jobs blaming damaging tax hikes on the sector.

The betting firm is conducting a review of their High Street estate across the UK and Ireland – as they launched an attack on the “material impact” of hiked levies.



The move comes on the back of Betfred planning to close 132 shops and William Hill and 888 owner Evoke shutting 270 stores.

Its follow ex-Chancellor Rachel Reeves increasing the duty rate on gaming machines found in betting stores and a new online sports betting duty coming in next year.



Shadow Sport Minister Louie French said: “Labour’s morality police and economic incompetence continue to destroy high street jobs every week.

“We warned the Government this would be the consequence of their disastrous policies and it is consumers, sports and workers who will pay the price.

The rise of the online illegal black market and decline in regulated businesses is a lose, lose situation for Government and UK sport.”

The Sun’s Save Our Bets campaign urged ministers not to raise betting duties at the Budget.

Blame for the pending closures in the UK was also laid at rising costs with firms hit by added national insurance contributions and rising energy bills.

The firm has not said how many closures there would be across the two countries.



Grainne Hurst, boss of the Betting and Gaming Council said: “This is yet more evidence of the real-world consequences of the tax rises imposed on Britain’s betting and gaming industry.

“The sector repeatedly warned that higher taxes would lead to shop closures, job losses and less investment, and sadly that is exactly what we are now seeing.

“Since the last Budget alone, more than 640 betting shops have now closed and around 5,000 jobs have been lost across the sector.”

Betting shops have also been in the firing line under Prime Minister Andy Burnham who is looking at making it harder for councils to stop new betting shops from opening.

A spokesperson from Flutter UK and Ireland, which owns Paddy Power, said its high street estate remains a key part of its business across the UK and Ireland.



They added: “Unfortunately, we have had to take the extremely difficult decision to conduct this review.

“The high street trading environment has been challenging for a number of years given rising costs, fierce competition, economic uncertainty and the shift to online but we also face a material impact from the higher gambling taxes announced in last year’s UK Budget.”

A government spokesperson said: “The gambling sector is supported by a stable economy and it must contribute to public services.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Gambling duty reforms will raise around £1 billion a year to help fund the government’s priorities, including support with the cost of living.

“We are also providing millions in additional funding to Gambling Commission to strengthen enforcement and tackle illegal gambling.”

News.title: Desperate sister fears missing Brit, 23, was ‘kidnapped’ on family holiday after vanishing on party boat in Lisbon
News.content:
HOLIDAY NIGHTMARE Desperate sister fears missing Brit, 23, was ‘kidnapped’ on family holiday after vanishing on party boat in Lisbon

A BRITISH family fear a 23-year-old university student was taken after he mysteriously vanished from a party boat at a Brit holiday hotspot.

Julian Amaral disappeared during a white party aboard the Vida De Jovem, meaning “life of a young person”, after boarding the vessel with his cousin.



His heartbroken sister Jennifer Amaral, 34, told The Sun: “I was so shocked when I found out about all of this. I really thought we would’ve found him by now!

“My theory is that he’s been taken… this is definitely unprovoked.



“He could have been an easy target because he doesn’t speak the language.”

Julian, from High Wycombe, Buckinghamshire, had been on holiday with his family when he disappeared in Lisbon, Portugal, around midnight yesterday.



The university student was last heard from by his mum on Tuesday, when he told her he would be attending the white party on a boat in Lisbon, Portugal.

After boarding the vessel, Julian told his 24-year-old cousin that he was going to the toilet.

As music blared, Julian supposedly made his way down to the urinal in the basement of the boat at around 11.25pm and has not been seen since.

The student’s phone location froze at almost exactly the same time he told his cousin he was going to the toilet.



It remains stuck showing him in the middle of the ocean.

As the boat neared the dock, his cousin – who had been busy socialising – realised Julian had been gone for some time.

He frantically began searching for him before calling other family members in a panic.



The family raced to where the boat was docked before launching a desperate search through the surrounding area.

At around midnight, they tore through nightclubs, street corners and restaurants where Julian might have gone.

Their first stop was Docks, a bar where boat parties usually end, but there was no sign of him.

After around an hour, the family reported him to police.

The case has now been moved into a criminal investigation after the 24-hour timeframe passed.



Several witnesses have since claimed they saw Julian get off the boat when it docked back in Lisbon.

Two security guards are among those who reportedly saw him disembark.

Another witness contacted Jennifer on social media and said she had spoken to Julian and also saw him get off the vessel.



Jennifer said police searched the boat but found no trace of her brother.

Tearing up on the phone, she said: “We told the police and the police went to search the boat but there was no sign of him at all.

“Not a lot could be done because of the time the incident took place.”

She added: “It’s all happened very unexpectedly. It’s all very unusual to me.”

Cops have also checked the nearest hospitals in case Julian took himself there or was taken there by someone else.



But the family plans to search the hospitals themselves again as the desperate hunt continues.

In a heartbreaking message to Julian, Jennifer said: “He has such a bright future ahead of him and he is one of the friendliest people people you will ever meet.

“He is the most kind-hearted person in my life. Just so bubbly and personable.

“He is so loved, he’s got nieces and nephews who are hurting.

“My mum is really hurting. We just want someone to come across him and say something to us.



“We miss him and we love him and we just want him to be back safely.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Jennifer is urging anyone with more information to come forward and contact her.

News.title: Cop and colleague changed sexuality of her ex-husband on official police records as ‘juvenile prank’
News.content:
COP 'JOKE' Cop and colleague changed sexuality of her ex-husband on official police records as ‘juvenile prank’

A COP and her colleague changed the sexuality of her ex-husband on official records as a “juvenile prank”.

Sergeant Sophie Watterson-Jones, 36, and Constable Mark Hempsall, 58, accessed the police computer to tweak the existing “no entry” box to “homosexual”.



The pair have now pleaded guilty to the unauthorised modification of police computer data under the Computer Security Act.

Watterson-Jones’ ex told the court it would be “highly embarrassing” for him if something appeared claiming he was gay.



He said in a victim impact statement that as a Muslim, he would have to explain he was straight.

The man added: “This worries me. I should not be in this position.”



Magistrates in the Isle of Man were told that the so-called prank came to light when messages on Watterson-Jones’ phone were downloaded.

Hempsall wrote in one “You like this” as Watterson-Jones replied: “That made me giggle.”

She continued: “Love it”.

The court heard Hempsall had instigated the offence but, as his superior officer, Watterson-Jones should have stopped him.



Prosecutor Harry Bellis said the tweak appeared to be a joke between the two defendants.

“But of course modification of data of that nature is not a joke and the consequences are taken seriously”, he added.

Both officers were fined £2,000 and each ordered each to pay £500 prosecution costs.

Sentencing, magistrates said: “As police officers you should have known better.

“While this may be looked at by some as a juvenile prank you were both serving police officers.



‘The real damage here is the impact which these offences have on the public’s trust and confidence in the Isle of Man Constabulary.”

An Isle of Man Constabulary spokesperson said: “The Isle of Man Constabulary notes the outcome of the court proceedings concerning the serving police officers.

“The Constabulary is considering the implications of the court’s findings and any consequential internal processes. It would be inappropriate to comment further while those matters remain ongoing.”

News.title: Putin warns Russians they must be ‘prepared for anything’ as tyrant quietly expands his deadliest drone factory
News.content:
VLADIMIR Putin has warned Russians to be “prepared for anything” after admitting – for the first time – that the Kremlin was “mistaken” to believe Ukraine won’t hit oil refineries.

The Russian President gave no hope of an end to his invasion, and instead vowed to unleash more retaliatory strikes so “they don’t harm us again.”



“We must be prepared for anything,” he said during the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok when asked if the current long fuel queues – caused by Ukrainian drone strikes – were here to stay.

“Only our readiness for anything will give everyone who wants to harm us an understanding that it is better not to do so.”



The dictator added: “(We) assumed that they were purely civilian facilities, and they could not be targets of any attacks even in conditions of armed conflict.”

This comes just days after Putin smirked as he refused to rule out strikes on military sites in the UK.

His thinly veiled threat came after Andy Burnham gave Ukraine blueprints for long-range Storm Shadow missiles – sparking a furious response from Moscow.

NATO leaders have already warned that the Kremlin is already waging an increasingly aggressive “hybrid” campaign of sabotage, cyberattacks and disinformation across Europe – so fears are growing of further escalation.

At the same time, suspected Russian incursions and plots have raised the danger of a miscalculation invoking NATO’s Article 5 collective-defence guarantee.

While sweet-talking the crowd at Vladivostok, Putin failed to mention that he is beefing up production at his notorious drone base in Yelabuga.



Satellite images circulated by Copernicus reveal the massive expansion at the secretive drone hub in the Alabuga Special Economic Zone where the lethal Geran drones are being manufactured.

Based on the Iranian-developed Shahed drones, they are regularly used in attacks against Ukraine.

It is understood that the expansion of the factory now covers more than 1,000 hectares, Bild reported.



A protective barrier is intended to prevent Ukrainian drones from hitting the important arms facility.

Analysis by the US think tank CSIS estimated the reported production at more than 5,500 drones per month.

While ramping up arms production, experts have argued that Russia is readying to unveil a new wave of mobilisation after elections due later this month.



“There is no such scenario today that would require mobilisation,” Putin insisted.

At the same time, he also ruled out peace talks, citing Western seizures of his shadow fleet tankers used to illegally transport oil.

“From the seizure of civilian vessels, to strikes on civilian merchant ships,” Putin said.

“And now, all the more so, we have heard threats of attacks on civilian aircraft. This is, of course, a manifestation of state terrorism.

“And this undoubtedly complicates, seriously complicates, the possibility of holding bilateral peace talks [to end the war in Ukraine].”



This comes as Norwegian authorities have seized a Russian cruise ship in the Arctic on behalf of Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Officials said the vessel, ⁠the Professor Molchanov, was seized late last night in Barentsburg, a coal mining settlement that Russia operates on the Norwegian Arctic archipelago of Svalbard under the terms of a 1920 treaty.

Russia called the arrest of the ship an act of piracy and said it had summoned the Norwegian ambassador to deliver a strong protest.

News.title: Guinness depot raided as brazen thieves steal 70,000 pints worth £115k
News.content:
Guinness depot raided as brazen thieves steal 70,000 pints worth £115k

Police said the thieves took off with two HGV trailers filled with £115,000 worth of Guinness - equalling 70,000 pints - at an industrial estate in Runcorn, Cheshire

View 2 Images Two HGV trailers carrying more than 800 barrels were spotted at the scene (Image: doram via Getty Images)

More than than 70,000 pints worth of Guinness has been stolen by thieves who took two HGV trailers from a depot, police have said.

‌



The trailers were carrying around 800 barrels of the stout - worth an estimated £115,000 - before they were driven away from an industrial estate in Runcorn on Monday, a Cheshire Constabulary spokesman said.

‌



Officers are now appealing for witnesses who may have seen a lorry entering the Aston Lane area at about 7.45pm, to contact them.

‌



The vehicle is said to have connected to an HGV trailer containing the Guinness before leaving the site at around 7.55pm and driving towards the Mersey Gateway bridge.

A second lorry arrived at 9.12pm and connected to another trailer, which also contained barrels of Guinness. That lorry left at 9.30pm and headed in the direction of Rainhill and Watkinson Way.

View 2 Images The trailers were carrying around 800 barrels of Guinness (Image: Cheshire Constabulary/PA Wire)

‌



The stolen HGVs are believed to have been driven away by men, police said. The first driver is described as white with a short dark beard and he was wearing a beanie hat, while the second is believed to have been wearing a cap.

Detectives say the barrels, containing around 70,400 pints of the Irish tipple, had been intended to be delivered to pubs.

Diageo, which owns Guinness, has a packaging warehouse on the Whitehouse Industrial Estate on Aston Lane. It is estimated the total value of the items stolen - the Guinness and the trailers themselves - is around £205,000.

Article continues below

The missing trailers are described as white tri-axle curtain side trailers with branding for logistics company GXO on their curtains and rear doors.

The trucks have the unique ID numbers DL736 and DL542 on the top left corner of their rear doors.

Cheshire Constabulary has appealed for anyone with information, or any drivers who may have dashcam footage, to contact them on the website, or by calling 101 and using incident reference number IML-2408641.

News.title: Reform's Zia Yusuf branded 'racist clown' by Piers Morgan after post about Labour politician
News.content:
Reform's Zia Yusuf branded 'racist clown' by Piers Morgan after post about Labour politician

Reform's home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf has come under fire after attacking a Labour politician tipped to stand in a by-election to replace Keir Starmer next month

View 3 Images Zia Yusuf sparked a backlash after attacking the leader of Camden Council, who came to the UK as a child refugee (Image: Getty)

A senior Reform figure has been dismissed as a "racist clown" by Piers Morgan after attacking a Labour politician tipped to stand in Keir Starmer's old seat.

‌



Zia Yusuf, who describes himself as shadow home secretary despite not being an MP, shared a picture of Camden Council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali and whined that she was born in Somalia. London Labour MPs have called on Reform to condemn the comment, and said police should assess whether it should be treated as inciting hatred.

‌



Ms Abdi-Wali, a governor at two local schools and a volunteer and trustee at charities in North London, has been linked with the vacant Holborn and St Pancras constituency. A by-election will be held next month after Mr Starmer announced he was stepping down.

‌



On Wednesday evening Mr Yusuf wrote: "The front runner being foisted on the people of Holborn by Labour to replace the former Prime Minister Keir Starmer in our Parliament was born in Somalia. Do you understand what’s happening?"

View 3 Images Piers Morgan branded Mr Yusuf a racist clown (Image: BBC)

It sparked a wave of condemnation, with TV host Mr Morgan responded: "So disgusting. You’re the son of Sri Lankan Muslim immigrants to the UK, you racist clown."

‌



Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey wrote: "This is racism, straight out of the Trump playbook. Reform are trying to turn our great country into a franchise of Trump's America. There are countless British patriots who came here from overseas, many of them refugees we proudly welcomed. That's the kind of country we are."

Labour MP Dawn Butler and fellow London MPs have written to Reform's chairman, Lee Anderson urging the party to act. In the letter, shared on social media, she wrote: "We condemn his post, which we believe to be racist, in the strongest possible terms.

"Councillor Sagal Abdi-Wali is British, who came to this country as a child refugee and has lived here for decades. She has served her community with dedication as a local councillor and is now the leader of Camden Council. Her story is inspiring, and one we should be proud of.

‌



View 3 Images Mr Yusuf made the remark about Camden Council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali

"To suggest that her place of birth should somehow determine whether she is fit to represent Holburn and St Pancras in Parliament is deeply offensive, divisive and wrong. It is exactly the kind of politics that we should reject.

"Following the horrific murder of Ann Widdecombe, and at a time when abuse toward politicans is sadly on the rise, this rhetoric is dangerous and irresponsible."

‌



And it went on to urge the Met Police to look at whether the post meets the threshold for stirring up racial hatred. The letter states: "We also urge the Metropolitan Police to assess whether the post meets the legal threshold for an offence of stirring up racial hatred. That is a matter for the police to determine, but allegations of this nature must be taken seriously."

Ms Abdi-Wali arrived in Camden as a child refugee, and has lived in the borough most of her life. Before becoming council leader she was the authority's cabinet member for housing.

On Thursday morning Nigel Farage's number two, Richard Tice, struggled to defend his colleague. Asked on Times Radio what Mr Yusuf meant, he said: "It's a question of if that person is selected, it's a question of fact, whether they're born in Somalia or not." And pressed further, he said: "Frankly, that is of little interest to voters up and down the country."

Article continues below

And Mr Tice continued: "At the end of the day, everybody is their own individual. I don't control other people's tweets and they don't control my tweets. You know, we do live in a free country and a free society."

The Mirror has contacted Reform UK for comment.

News.title: ‘Dangerous’ man who filmed himself sexually assaulting woman while she slept is jailed
News.content:
‘Dangerous’ man who filmed himself sexually assaulting woman while she slept is jailed

Kenan Samuel, 28, invited a woman to his home in Cambridgeshire for drinks before sexually assaulting her while she slept and filming the depraved act

View Image Kenan Samuel, 28, has been jailed (Image: Cambridgeshire Police)

A "dangerous" and "cunning" man who filmed himself sexually assaulting a woman has been jailed for five years

‌



Kenan Samuel, 28, invited the victim to his home in Alconbury Weald, Cambridgeshire, for drinks along with another man on December 18, 2020. The woman had gone to bed and fallen asleep in the early hours of the morning.

‌



Samuel then got into the bed and began touching her. He filmed himself sexually assaulting the victim, who was unconscious and unable to consent.

‌



After he was reported to the police, his phone was seized and police discovered that he had also sent himself a nude image of the victim from her phone without her permission.

Samuel tried to cover his tracks by deleting the message from the victim's phone so she would not see that the photo had been sent.

‌



At Peterborough Crown Court on Friday, August 28, Samuels, of Lysons Close, Alconbury Weald, was jailed for five years.

He admitted to assaulting a female by penetration with part of body/a thing, voyeurism, and causing a computer to perform a function to secure/enable unauthorised access to a program/data, reports Cambridgeshire Live.

DC Sally Muntane-Crane, who investigated, said: "Samuel is a dangerous man who took advantage of the victim when she was in a vulnerable state.

Article continues below

"He was also cunning, deleting the evidence he had sent himself a nude photo from the victim's phone without her consent.

"I would like to praise the victim for reporting what happened, and for showing tremendous strength and bravery during the investigation.

"I hope it gives confidence to other victims to come forward, knowing they will be listened to, and the police and wider criminal justice system will do everything they can to get justice for them."

News.title: Donald Trump could be gearing up to ambush Andy Burnham over the Falklands
News.content:
Is Donald Trump gearing up to ambush Andy Burnham at their first meeting? The pair are expected to sit down for the first time at the UN General Assembly in a few weeks - and the stakes are not inconsiderable. Burnham will be keen to take on Keir Starmer's mantle of Ukraine's defender - if not of Trump whisperer - and if he needs to dangle a little North Sea oil drilling to get the US President to play nice, so be it. Nice, simple international diplomacy with the bare minimum of drama. Right?

Well, maybe - because of late the Trump administration has been a little less studiously neutral than usual about a pretty contentious issue - the Falkland Islands. Internal memos have suggested the US position on the Islands could be reviewed - especially in light of Trump still being cross with us for not running to his heel when he went to bomb Iran, and pre-emptively mad at us for not spending enough on defence.

"I always review every position - that's just one of many," Trump said on Monday when he was asked about the Falklands directly.

And right on cue, Trump's diminutive, chainsaw wielding buddy Javier Milei - Argentina's President - is doing a TV address on the subject of the islands on Thursday night. Trump has been doing all sorts of things to try and prop up Milei - a kindred spirit. That includes importing a ton of Argentine beef, much to the annoyance of American cattle herders.

‌



Perhaps this is another gift from Trump to Milei - backing him in a fight that he probably can't win, but could make him look pretty badass to the people of Argentina. Trump, after all, isn't at all bothered about maintaining relations with America's traditional allies. And he's considerably more bothered about forging new alliances within his bubble of the Americas.

And last night, Trump made an even more straightforward threat. Asked whether he'd come to Britain's aid if the Islands were under threat from Argentina, he said: "I was there when they had the first war, that was a long time ago... you comported yourself very well, took it back very shortly. But it is a long way away.

"So, your country's not doing well. Don't forget you get a big percentage of your oil from the Strait of Hormuz and you weren't there to help me. Your country was not there to help me."

On the other hand... it wouldn't be such a bad thing for Burnham either. He would get to defend Britain's claim to the Falklands against an Argentinian madman and a US President that pretty much everyone in the UK loathes. There's really no downside. So maybe...bring it on?

‌

News.title: Andy Burnham vows to 'scale up' efforts with France to stop small boat crossings
News.content:
Andy Burnham vows to 'scale up' efforts with France to stop small boat crossings

Speaking on Thursday, the new PM praised the cooperation between Britain and France in dealing with the crisis, and claimed it was helping deter people from making the perilous journey across the Channel

View 2 Images Andy Burnham praised the work done with France to deter small boats (Image: WIktor Szymanowicz/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Andy Burnham has vowed to "scale up" a crackdown on small boats as he welcomed the French President Emmanuel Macron to Downing Street.

‌



Speaking on Thursday, the new PM praised the cooperation between Britain and France in dealing with the crisis, and claimed it was helping deter people from making the perilous journey across the Channel.

‌



The two leaders met at No 10 on Thursday morning after spending the previous evening together at the British Museum alongside the King to mark the special exhibition of the Bayeux Tapestry.

‌



This week data released by the Home Office showed the lowest total crossings since 2019 and the lowest number of people reaching the UK since 2020. There were 7,416 arrivals between June 1 and August 30 - compared to 15,458 over the same period in 2022 and 12,421 in 2022 under the Tories.

Surge teams to tackle mega dinghies on French beaches as PM and Emmanuel Macron set to meet READ MORE :

Small boat crossings drop to seven-year low over summer despite hot weather READ MORE :

View 2 Images It comes after boat crossing numbers reached their lowest levels since 2019 (Image: CPS/PA Wire)

Speaking in Downing Street’s pillared room, Mr Burnham said it was “so fitting that it is our nearest neighbour and close friend Emmanuel” who was his first international guest since coming to power.

‌



He added: “It shows what collaboration can achieve, just as we are also showing on Ukraine, on small boats and also on strengthening the UK-EU relationship. So I look forward to discussing those themes further with you today.”

Mr Macron said: “This is a very strong relationship. For me it is extremely important, and I’m here with willingness and a commitment to get closer.”

Ahead of the talks, Mr Burnham said the two countries must “stay one step ahead” of the criminal gangs’ evolving tactics to transport people across the English Channel, and he vowed not to be “complacent” after a fall in the number of small boat arrivals.

‌



No 10 said measures to counter the trend include deploying a surge team of 45 officers to French western beaches in the coming weeks, almost tripling resources in the area.

Speaking after the meeting, a Downing Street spokeswoman said: "The Prime Minister began by thanking President Macron for France's loan of the Bayeux Tapestry, which he said symbolised common bonds between the UK and France, and was a statement of unity in an increasingly divided world.

"Turning to small boats, the Prime Minister said the cooperation between both countries was clearly working and operational teams were making headway on driving down numbers and reducing crossings.

‌



"It was now vital to ensure that success was scaled up across Europe to deter illegal migration, the leaders agreed.”

However, Refugee charity Freedom from Torture said ministers should improve the asylum system instead of supporting policing in France.

Head of asylum advocacy Sile Reynolds said: “The number of people crossing the Channel is dropping, but as smugglers adapt, crossings are only becoming more dangerous.

Article continues below

“At the most basic level, the Government is failing to protect the lives of vulnerable people seeking safety. UK taxpayers’ money is being spent bolstering police activity in northern France despite accounts of brutal violence against refugees.”

News.title: Direct Line home insurance is now on comparison websites - but it may not be cheapest
News.content:
Direct Line home insurance is now on comparison websites - but it may not be cheapest

The insurance company is rolling out three home insurance products across Confused.com and will expand to other websites from later this month

View 2 Images Home insurance covers you if something bad happens to your property (Image: ijeab via Getty Images)

Direct Line home insurance is launching on comparison websites for the first time.

‌



The insurance company is rolling out three products across Confused.com and will expand to other websites from later this month. Home insurance covers you if something bad happens to your property, such as a fire, burglary or storm damage.

‌



It is not a legal requirement in the UK, though most mortgage lenders will expect you to have it as part of the terms of your loan. The three main types are buildings, contents and combined buildings and contents insurance.

‌



The update from Direct Line means shoppers will have more choice when comparing insurance policies, although it does not mean that its policies will be the cheapest.

It comes after Direct Line launched its car insurance products on comparison websites in 2024. At the time, the company said it planned on extending its availability.

It had stated that 90% of consumers visit comparison websites when deciding on insurance. The company will continue to sell products directly to consumers.

‌



View 2 Images Direct Line home insurance is launching on comparison websites

Adam Winslow, chief executive at Direct Line Group, said: "We are delivering a key pillar of our corporate strategy, demonstrating how we can move at pace to meet the changing needs of our customers."

Matt Pernet, Commercial Director, Direct Line Retail PCW, at Aviva, said: "Making Direct Line home insurance available through price comparison websites for the first time is an important step in giving customers more choice in how they buy cover.

‌



“We know customers have different needs and preferences when purchasing home insurance, so we want to make it easier for them to buy through the channel that suits them best, while continuing to benefit from products designed to help protect their homes and possessions."

If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Money newsletter here for all the best advice and shopping deals straight to your inbox.

Steve Dukes, CEO at Confused.com, said: “We’re delighted to be chosen by Aviva to exclusively launch Direct Line’s home insurance products on price comparison websites.

‌



“Direct Line is an exciting addition to our current offering of leading insurance brands in the home insurance market, allowing us to offer a broader choice of policy types and prices to customers.

“Consumers continue to use price comparison to find the right insurance for them. We’re pleased to support Aviva’s strategic ambitions to successfully launch Direct Line home insurance on price comparison, increasing its visibility to a wider pool of customers while bringing even more choice to our platform.”

Save money on home insurance

Money Saving Expert says 21 days before your home insurance is due to expire is the prime time to find the cheapest deals. If you have found cheaper quotes, talk to your existing home insurance provider to see if they can beat it.

Article continues below

If they can't offer you a better price, you can switch to another provider when your existing cover ends. When you search for insurance, you are normally asked to share your job title.

It is important not to lie on your insurance application, otherwise you would be committing fraud, but sometimes changing your job title to something that can legitimately be used to describe your occupation could save you money.

News.title: Queen Camilla returns to riding school she opened 25 years ago to visit one of late Queen's horses
News.content:
Queen Camilla returns to riding school she opened 25 years ago to visit one of late Queen's horses

Queen Camilla has visited a London riding school, which is home to one of the late Queen's Elizabeth's former horses, where she fed the animals and praised the community initiative

View 5 Images Queen Camilla opened the centre 25 years ago, and returned today to see the new community space (Image: Henry Nicholls/PA Wire)

The Queen praised an inner city riding school as "bigger and better" than ever as she visited two of its new horses, including a fell pony that used to ride alongside the late Queen.

‌



On a visit to Ebony Riding Club in Brixton in south London, where she has been President since 2009, Camilla fed polo mints to 17-year-old Taylor, who escorted the late Queen Elizabeth and her beloved fell pony Emma on daily outings with her head groom Terry Pendry. Earlier this summer, Taylor, a 17-year-old black mare, moved to Brixton from the Royal Mews along with a former carriage horse called Margate, known affectionately as Maggie.

‌



"Where are my polos?", said a smiling Camilla as she was introduced to both animals, stopping to stroke and pat them and offer them the sweets.

‌



View 5 Images Camilla visited Ebony Riding Club in Brixton today (Image: Henry Nicholls/PA Wire)

Maggie, a Cleveland Bay bred at Hampton Court and raised as a carriage horse, worked at the Royal Mews until after the Coronation. An injury meant the horse was no longer well enough to pull carriages, but after a three-year break she has been loaned to the charity, alongside Taylor, and the two are now used to teach local children and young people how to ride and care for horses.

The Queen was shown inside the centre's stables, where bars separating the horses have been partially removed to allow them to socialise more. The change was made after one horse, Tommy, refused to lie down at night. But the more open environment has significantly improved the animals' wellbeing, resulting in better sleep for them all. "Tommy is much more relaxed and feels safe," volunteer Sarah Cope told the Queen.

‌



View 5 Images The Queen has been president of the organisation since 2009 (Image: Henry Nicholls/PA Wire)

Under the Equicentric Futures project, led by the Association of British Riding Schools, the nine resident horses have also been given slow feeder nets of hay to replicate natural foraging, which has the added bonus of making their food last longer overnight.

The Queen, who wore a white animal print dress by Fiona Clare, then met Year 6 pupils from Corpus Christi Primary School in Brixton Hill, who have taken part in the centre's schools' programme, learning to ride, groom and muck out stables.

‌



Headteacher Jean Connery told her: "It's wonderful for the children. They would never have the opportunity to do this and it's so good for their confidence. We are very lucky to have this on our doorstep."

The Queen, who opened the current centre 25 years ago, also met volunteers who have helped to create a new community space under a former railway arch at the centre and are training others to volunteer with the horses and community groups.

View 5 Images Camilla pet several horses during her day in South London (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



"It's such a lovely place, you must all get so much satisfaction," she said. Later, Camilla watched as Adam Bentallah, 12, on Taylor, and Isaiah Clayton, 16, on Maggie, gave a riding demonstration in the arena.

Afterwards, she presented them both with trophies in recognition of their hard work and dedication. Handing one to Isaiah, she called him a "star rider" and told Adam his award was "very well deserved". There was laughter as dogs nearby began to bark loudly, and she told the schoolboy: "Even the dogs are applauding you."

She said of the club, which celebrates its 30th anniversary this year: "It gets bigger and better every time. The first time I came here it was literally a field and a couple of stables."

‌



Jason Hawkes, 17, who has been attending the club as a rider and volunteer for eight years, presented the Queen with a bouquet of flowers. He said afterwards: "What it's done for me has been unbelievable. It's given me freedom and has opened my eyes to the world. There are so many other things you can do. It's good to get away from city life."

View 5 Images The Queen met with pupils from Corpus Christi Catholic School (Image: Henry Nicholls/PA Wire)

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Through access to horses, the charity works to improve the lives of some of the area's most disadvantaged children and young people aged 8 to 18. Several young riders have gone on to have a career in racing and this year several alumni will join the British Racing School, the National Stud and the National Horseracing College.

Chief Operating Officer Sid Holdsworth described the Queen's visit as "just so unbelievably special." He said: "She has always been such an incredibly supportive president, beyond what we would ever have hoped or expected, and we've been so lucky to see her so many times this year.

"So for her to make make the effort and come to Brixton is just incredible and so exciting. For our young people, it's just a once in a lifetime opportunity, and they think it is the coolest thing that we know the Queen."

News.title: Matt Lucas says ‘I’ve never spoken about this publicly’ as he reveals diagnosis
News.content:
Matt Lucas says ‘I’ve never spoken about this publicly’ as he reveals diagnosis

Former Little Britain and Great British Bake Off star Matt Lucas opened up about being diagnosed with a lifelong condition during a candid BBC Radio 2 interview.

View 4 Images Matt has revealed that he is autistic (Image: BBC)

Matt Lucas, 52, has revealed that he's been living with a neurodevelopmental condition for his entire life, but hasn't spoken about it in public until now.

‌



The Little Britain star told Romesh Ranganathan on BBC Radio 2: “I’ve never, ever spoken about this publicly, but I’m autistic, and so I enjoy periods of being very sociable, like you are in the theatre, and then I also enjoy those periods of solitude where I can just write on my own.”

‌



Romesh then asked Matt: "Do you find that you need to recharge each battery, like you're kind of flitting between those two things?"

‌



To which he replied: "Yeah, and so on my days off, you know you do theatre six days a week, and on my day off, apart from resting and resting my voice and all of that, on my day off I like not to see people and give them a break from me, but just to have that recharge time is quite important to me."

The NHS website states that being autistic can impact how you communicate with people and understand them, and how they understand you. The condition, which people are born with, can also affect how you think, learn and pay attention to things.

4 View 4 Images Matt accepting his OBE at Windsor Castle (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire) 4 View 4 Images Matt spoke to Romesh about his diagnosis (Image: Alan Chapman/Dave Benett/Getty I)

‌



Although still best-known for his work with David Walliams on sketch shows such as Little Britain and Come Fly With Me, Matt has also appeared in theatre productions including Les Misérables, Me and My Girl and – later this year – Matthew Bourne’s production of Oliver! At London’s Gielgud theatre, which co-stars Romesh’s son. .

Matt is also the author of two novels and is currently working on a third: “It’s for adults", he told Romesh. “The first two had been for kids, and it’s quite a long haul. I know what I want my fourth novel to be."

He’s also appeared in a long list of films, ranging from Paddington to Bridesmaids and Gladiator II.

‌



On stage, Matt says, he works hard at keeping things fresh and is always trying to discover new aspects of his character.: “I’ve played Thénardier in Les Misérables, on and off, for over 16 years. But every time, I try to find something new.

“I’m always finding new things in it,” he added, “And even 16 years on …I found things and thought, ‘Ah! Why have I never seen that before? That’s crazy. I’m going to play it like this…’

Matt adds that his ability to find new ways of playing a part is down to how well the writer has done their job; “If you’re in something that’s brilliant, and rich, and textured, that inspired other people in the show to keep their performances alive, and moveable, and evolving."

‌



“Then,” Matt adds, “your performance can evolve as well.”

Matt admitted that there are a couple of new roles that he would love to get his teeth into. He says that perhaps “one day” when he’s older he would like to play Tevye, the main character in Fiddler on the Roof.

View 4 Images Matt reunited with David Walliams for a podcast last year (Image: Dave Hogan/Getty Images)

‌



He also has an ambition to play Mrs. Lovett, the killer’s pie-making accomplice in Sweeney Todd: “I’ve never seen it played by a man before,” he told Romesh, “I don’t know if the Sondheim estate would permit it.”

He hasn’t entirely stopped working with his old Little Britain partner though. In 2025, Matt reunited with David Walliams to present a twice weekly podcast entitled Making a Scene, in which they interviewed interview showbiz pals such as Stephen Merchant, Jack Whitehall, Rob Brydon, Alan Carr and Richard E. Grant.

Announcing the podcast in a video posted on social media, the pair joked about past controversies, such as the use of racially stereotyped characters in Little Britain and Walliams’s notorious rudeness when he was a panellist on Britain’s Got Talent.

Article continues below

Matt is starring alongside Richard Ayoade, Isy Suttie, Nina Conti and Chloe Pettson on season 22 of Taskmaster, which begins on Thursday 3rd September from 9pm on Channel 4.

News.title: Burnham and Macron agree to scale up action on small boats in first meeting
News.content:
Macron said: "This is a very strong relationship. For me it is extremely important, and I'm here with willingness and a commitment to get closer."

The French leader's visit to the UK was primarily to mark the Bayeux Tapestry's loan to the British Museum. He met King Charles at the museum on Wednesday, ahead of the medieval tapestry going on public display next week.

In bilateral talks on Thursday, No 10 said Burnham and Macron agreed they were making headway in reducing small boat crossings in the English Channel but now needed to go further.

They also "discussed the UK's drive to get closer to Europe", while Burnham raised concerns about the potential impact of the Made in Europe procurement plan, being drawn up in Brussels to protect EU industries, on British sectors.

Burnham has previously called for closer ties with Europe, as had his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

The pair also discussed establishing local assembly lines in Ukraine for the Scalp long-range missile, a French version of the UK's Storm Shadow cruise missile.

The leaders also discussed the situation in the Middle East and the need to ensure de-escalation in the Strait of Hormuz.

And Burnham raised Israel's move to open up tenders for the construction of settlement homes in a strategically important part of the occupied West Bank, saying it was "unacceptable and only served to undermine the prospect of the two-state solution".

The development in the so-called E1 area would in effect divide the West Bank in two and isolate East Jerusalem.

Plans to build there have long been internationally condemned, with settlements illegal under international law.

The arrival of the first foreign leader under the Burnham premiership is an important symbolic moment - it shows the relationship with Paris is an important priority.

But it also reflects an obvious reality - to further reduce small boats crossings, working with France will be essential.

France and the UK have been working extremely closely on Ukraine and Iran, trying to jointly influence the White House.

And Paris will be an important player as the UK seeks even stronger economic ties with Europe under the new No 10 administration.

The "mega dinghies" crossing the Channel illegally - first seen earlier in August with a 15-metre long vessel carrying a record 230 migrants towards the UK - are arguably the most pressing challenge facing the pair.

It follows a summer when the number of small boat arrivals in the UK fell to a seven-year low.

News.title: Schools to close early for A66 crash funeral amid safety concerns
News.content:
Supt John Wrintmore from Cleveland Police said there was potential for traffic disruption and delays from 15:00 to 17:00 on Friday.

"This will affect areas of South Bank, Normanby Road through Teesville, Ormesby and Marton, and Acklam Road," he said.

"We are working closely with highways departments from the local authority, who are leading on the traffic management for this event, in order to minimise disruption.

"As with any significant gathering, we have plans in place to ensure public safety and security, which is line with our usual process."

A spokesperson for Redcar & Cleveland Borough Council said: "A number of schools in the South Bank area will close earlier than usual on Friday afternoon due to anticipated traffic congestion and transport disruption associated with a local funeral taking place in the area.

"The decision was made after careful consideration of the potential impact on home-to-school transport and the departure of pupils, staff and families at the end of the school day.

"Schools have worked with the Local Authority and transport providers to consider arrangements for pupils, including those who travel to and from specialist educational settings.

"We recognise that early closure may cause inconvenience for some parents and carers, and we thank them for their understanding and cooperation."

The decision comes after a vigil, for one of the young men who died, last week was followed by disorder in Haswell, County Durham, where a number of cars were set on fire.

The incident prompted criticism from MPs and police.

The Volkswagen Passat involved in the collision was being pursued by police until 10 seconds before the crash, according to the police watchdog.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct said the Passat was believed to be using cloned registration plates.

A total of 27 people have been arrested as part of a wider police operation against organised crime, following the crash.
