Sports.title: Chelsea ‘agreed £51million Manu Kone transfer before fateful Lamine Camara deadline drama but key condition was missed’
Sports.content:
CHELSEA reportedly came close to landing Manu Kone in the final days of the transfer window – only for Roma to pull the plug.

The West Londoners banked £125million when they flogged Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City on deadline day.



But Chelsea chief Xabi Alonso has been left short of options in the middle of the park after Monaco blocked Lamine Camara’s move at the 11th hour.

And it appears the Blues had already suffered a huge blow as they prepared to cash in on Fernandez.



L’Equipe report Chelsea agreed a money-spinning £51m deal to sign Kone, 25, from Roma.

But the Serie A giants were only prepared to finalise the paperwork if they brought in a replacement.

After failing to recruit Youssouf Fofana from AC Milan or Marseille’s Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg – who snubbed Newcastle’s advances earlier in the window – Roma told Chelsea that Kone would be going nowhere.

Alonso had already spoken to the midfielder about how he would be used when he arrived at Stamford Bridge.

Kone was also excited about the prospect of featuring in the Premier League for the first time.

But, having shone as France bagged fourth place at the World Cup during the summer, the ex-Borussia Monchengladbach man was forced to stay at Roma.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Giallorossi boss Gian Piero Gasperini refused to sanction Kone’s exit without filling the void as he prepares to face the likes of Paris Saint-Germain, Real Madrid and Manchester United in the Champions League.

It left Chelsea in limbo before suffering a deadline day disaster when their move for Camara fell through.

Blues chiefs are furious with Monaco after going against a verbal and written agreement to sell the Senegalese star, 22, at the last minute.

Camara’s cash-strapped employers rejected the chance to sign a deal sheet, meaning the swoop could not be revived when team-mate Folarin Balogun backed out of a move to Everton.



But Monaco chief executive Thiago Scuro has hit back by defending his club’s conduct.

Sports.title: Mike Dean 'nonsense' claims rubbished by former referees as FA urged to investigate
Sports.content:
Mike Dean 'nonsense' claims rubbished by former referees as FA urged to investigate

Controversial retired official Mike Dean's comments about his time as a Premier League referee has led to a strong reaction from two former top-flight officials

View 2 Images Mike Dean (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

Two former Premier League referees have criticised Mike Dean after the ex-official claimed to have played secret ‘games’ in matches during his time in the top flight. The former referee claimed that such games would involve waiting to see how long he could go without blowing the whistle or leaving the centre circle.

‌



Dean spent more than two decades as a referee in English football before retiring from the profession in 2022, and went on to spend a further year as a video assistant referee.

‌



During an appearance on Jamie Vardy's Having a Party podcast, Dean said: "There used to be games that we used to have, as a laugh, we used to say, 'Right, we'll kick off now, right? See how long we can go without blowing a whistle.'

‌



"Done that a few times in the Premier, before VAR obviously. Went 20–25 minutes without blowing a whistle a few times. Let it go, let it go, let it go.

Hugh Jackman reveals talks to buy into Championship club to rival Ryan Reynolds READ MORE :

Ismaila Sarr dream transfer amid Liverpool interest as stance perfectly clear READ MORE :

"I used to do another thing in the Premier League. I used to stand in the centre circle and see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about. The lads used to be on the line saying 'you can't'. I said 'I'll try it'. I just used to run around but don't come out of it. Got about 15 minutes once in one game, without leaving the centre circle."

Such comments have caused some outrage among the football community with calls for the FA to launch an investigation, while two former referees have openly criticised Dean as a result.

‌



Former Premier League referee Graham Scott labelled the claims from Dean about games within matches as ‘nonsense’.

“I worked with Mike [Dean] loads at times, they’re not true stories,” Scott told talkSPORT.

“It’s kind of the audio equivalent of clickbait isn’t it, to try and get people interested and laughing. It’s palpable nonsense.

‌



“Mike Dean [was] of course an outstanding ref, but it makes it so much harder when retired referees either bash their former colleagues for the sake of it.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“It’s fine to criticise, I do that, but do it with a bit of context and a bit of empathy.”

Scott later added: “I challenge Mike and say, ‘Okay, would you stand in front of the current refs and repeat all of those things?’

“And of course he wouldn’t, because they’re not true.”

‌



Mark Halsey, another former Premier League referee, was in disbelief at the comments made by Dean.

“All my years as a professional referee, I have to say I’ve never heard of these games. Never,” Halsey told BBC Sport.

View 2 Images Mike Dean (Image: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images)

‌

“And I have to say that I have never, ever thought about playing any sort of game, going out to referee.

“Because they’re massive games, you’ve got the fans, you’ve got the players, you’ve got the managers, the delegates, the coaches.

‌



“So I’m astounded, and if Mike has played these games, then he’s done that on his own accord.

“And if he has, then I think we need to know what games he’s done them in? How many games he’s done them in?

“And it brings into question the integrity of every official.”

Sports.title: Arsenal medical underway with third Gunners signing already lined up for 2027
Sports.content:
Arsenal medical underway with third Gunners signing already lined up for 2027

Arsenal are sorting a medical for FC Kolkheti-1913 Poti teenager Andria Bartishvili, with the 17-year-old set to sign a five-year contract and officially join the Premier League champions in 2027

View Image Mikel Arteta could add another youngster to his Arsenal squad next summer (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Arsenal are closing in on the signing of FC Kolkheti-1913 Poti star Andria Bartishvili, with the playmaker having a medical today. The Gunners have spent the summer preparing their squad for another Premier League title challenge, but have also had an eye on the future with deals to sign stars for the future.

‌



As has been reported by football.london, Arsenal have agreed a €4.5million (£3.9million) deal to sign the 17-year-old playmaker, although he will not move to the Emirates Stadium this summer.

‌



Instead, it’s understood that Bartishvili will officially become an Arsenal player in 12 months time, which will also coincide with the arrivals of Ecuadorian twins Holger and Edwin Quintero from Independiente.

‌



This will also be when Bartishvili turns 18, where he will be expected to sign a five-year contract to move to Arsenal.

Arsenal deal for Bruno Guimaraes rated one out of 10 in brutal transfer ranking READ MORE :

It is understood that Bartishvili was present at the Sobha Realty Training Centre on Thursday to undergo a medical and finalise the remaining details surrounding his switch to the Gunners.

The youngster is set to become the fourth young talent snapped up by Arsenal ahead of a prospective future arrival, following Victor Ozhianvuna's move from Shamrock Rovers in January.

‌



Georgian football expert Saba Sapanadze spoke to football.london regarding Arsenal's quest to sign Bartishvili, and why the fee agreed for the playmaker represents exceptional value for the Premier League champions.

“I think Arsenal were very lucky to get Andria for €4.5million,” Sapanadze said. “That only happened because he’s Georgian, otherwise I genuinely believe his price would have been around €15million-€20million.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



“Why? Because he is considered one of the biggest talents in the country, alongside [Khvicha] Kvaratskhelia’s brother, Tornike.”

Sapanadze runs Geo Team, a Georgian football platform that delivers updates on players from the country, and proceeded to outline why he anticipates Bartishvili will join the first team in training upon his arrival next year, after which a loan could be an option.

“Let’s be realistic. Arsenal have an incredible squad right now, so it would be unrealistic for me to tell you that he’ll walk straight into the first team,” he said.

‌



“However, from what I understand, he’ll have a first-team contract and will train with the senior squad.

“Perhaps, initially, a loan to the Championship for regular playing time could be a smart move and help him adapt to British football.”

‌



Arsenal experienced a relatively quiet summer transfer window following their Premier League title success earlier this year, with four new additions confirmed by the club.

Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa, Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier have all been brought in by Arsenal this summer, as Mikel Arteta and Co. look to retain their crown.

Sports.content:
Ismaila Sarr dream transfer amid Liverpool interest as stance perfectly clear

Liverpool registered an interest in the Crystal Palace winger during the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Ismaila Sarr revealed his dream Premier League transfer (Image: Sebastian Frej/Getty Images)

Ismaila Sarr declared his love for Manchester United before Liverpool held an interest in signing him. The Crystal Palace winger was the subject of transfer speculation as Anfield chiefs searched for another wide forward in the summer transfer window.

‌



Andoni Iraola eventually secured his key target, Bradley Barcola, signing the ex-Paris Saint-Germain star for an eye-watering £123million. However, Sarr was among the targets on the Liverpool manager's wishlist, along with Brighton's Yankuba Minteh.

‌



The Reds pivoted to the Senegal international after they failed in a move for Minteh. However, Sarr admitted during the summer that his dream transfer was actually one of Liverpool's biggest rivals.

‌



Speaking during the World Cup, the winger admitted: "My dream club? Honestly, there is only one club. I love Manchester United with all my heart, and I am one of its biggest fans.

‌



Sarr left the door wide open for a move to Old Trafford and reports claimed that talks had been held regarding a potential transfer. Liverpool continued their pursuit for Sarr, which would've cost them around £50m, but ultimately secured their main target in Barcola.

Despite his love for United, Pierre Sage admitted that Sarr will need time to recover from his failed move to Anfield. The Palace boss said: "He has to digest for sure because it's a dream for a lot of players to play with this kind of club.

Sports.title: 5 worst footballing opinions given new 'walk of shame' award by Alan Shearer
Sports.content:
5 worst footballing opinions given new 'walk of shame' award by Alan Shearer

Alan Shearer has been granted a star on the 'Walk of Shame' outside Wembley Stadium for one of his worst football opinions in a new tongue-in-cheek installation

View 3 Images Alan Shearer hopes his prediction was just 12 months early rather than wrong (Image: Betfair)

Alan Shearer is among the pundits and former players who have been granted stars on Betfair's newly launched 'Walk of Shame' on Wembley Way outside the national stadium.

‌



However, his claim that Newcastle United would beat Sunderland in both of last season's Tyne–Wear derbies - before they lost each game - does not make the top five of worst football opinions of all time. The ranking is based on research conducted with YouGov, which polled 2,008 adult fans across Great Britain.

‌



Alan Hansen and Roy Keane, however, do feature. Two of the takes are about Erling Haaland, with content creators included as well.

‌



Alan Shearer confirms real reason he is scaling back BBC Match of the Day appearances READ MORE :

Alan Shearer leaves Bruno Guimaraes in no doubt after leaving Newcastle for Arsenal READ MORE :

Number five is Hansen's infamous phrase, "You can't win anything with kids". It was uttered on Match of the Day about Manchester United after Sir Alex Ferguson's young side lost 3-1 against Aston Villa on the opening day of the 1995/96 season.

Despite having an average age of 26 years and 137 days - when considering players who made 10 or more appearances - they won the Premier League and FA Cup double. They were the youngest to do so for almost a decade, until Jose Mourinho's first Chelsea team won the title with an average age of 25 years and 312 days.

Coming in at four is 'Rory Talks Football ', an Arsenal supporter who said last year that the Gunners "finishing second was a better achievement than Leicester City winning the league". The Gunners were not 5000/1 with bookmakers to come second when they achieved that 'feat', that is for sure.

‌



3 View 3 Images Alan Shearer avoided his take making the top five, unlike 'Humzy' and 'Rory Talks Football' (Image: Betfair) 3 View 3 Images Alan Shearer joked "What fool said that?" when reading the quote on his star on Betfair's 'Walk of Shame' (Image: Betfair)

Third is where Keane fell for when he said Haaland is "almost like a League Two player". He made the comparison two years ago after a 0-0 draw between Arsenal and Manchester City.

‌



However, it is worth noting that the pundit drew those parallels when discussing his poor general play. In the same breath, he said that "in front of the goal, he's the best in the world ".

The top two are reserved for content creators, with Man United fan 'Humzy' in second for saying last year that "Ruben Amorim's legacy at Man United will be greater than Pep Guardiola's at Man City". Rory Jennings takes top spot for simply saying in 2022 that "Haaland will flop in the Premier League".

"It will be a more challenging season for Sunderland this year than it was last year. I do think it will be tougher times for Newcastle as well, and we'll have to be patient, so let's wait and see. We all think we know what's going to happen. But even the best of us can completely miss the mark."

Sports.title: Alexander Isak and £35m goal machine will have Man Utd excited after last-minute deal
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak and £35m goal machine will have Man Utd excited after last-minute deal

Chido Obi has joined Eredivisie side Willem II, following in the footsteps of £125million signing Alexander Isak and Manchester United have every reason to be excited for the future

View Image Chido Obi has left Man United on loan (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United sealed a loan move for Chido Obi on deadline day, and the reflections of Alexander Isak and Benfica star Vangelis Pavlidis on their own breakthroughs at Willem II will give the club real optimism about his development. The 18‑year‑old joined the Dutch side after making eight senior appearances for United.

‌



Isak, who became a British transfer‑record signing when he joined Liverpool from Newcastle United for £125million last summer, spent a season on loan at Willem II from Borussia Dortmund after struggling for regular minutes in Germany. Arriving in Tilburg at 20, he described that spell as 'the most important season of my career', saying the pressure to deliver became the catalyst for everything that followed.

‌



He spoke about the value of minutes and how the club gave him the platform to prove himself when opportunities elsewhere were limited. "That season at Willem II was the most important season of my career," Isak previously said.

‌



Fenerbahce issue Mason Greenwood statement as UEFA investigate ex-Man Utd star READ MORE :

Eight players Man Utd could lose for NOTHING with urgent talks planned READ MORE :

"Because that step, knowing I had to deliver, it's what made everything else possible. In football, you never know when the next chance is going to come, and so you take it.

"Obviously, as a young player, you need time on the pitch. If you're not getting that, all you can do is train harder... I knew my chance would come, even if it wasn't there, I knew it would come at another club and I wanted to be ready."

Greek forward Pavlidis followed a similar path, joining the Eredivisie side on loan from VfL Bochum at the age of 20. "Willem II was very important for my career," he recalled.

‌



"I was still looking for my position on the pitch, at that time I wasn't a number 9 yet. [So] to be at a club in the Eredivisie, to play and score goals in the league, to play the cup final, the European competitions, it was incredible."

Pavlidis went on to spend three years at AZ Alkmaar before making the switch to Lisbon to strengthen Portuguese giants Benfica in 2024. He has scored 71 goals in 118 Liga Portugal appearances to date.

‌



Earlier this summer, Pavlidis was linked with a Premier League move, with Tottenham and Aston Villa both reported to be interested in the striker. Serie A pair AC Milan and Roma also explored potential deals.

Barcelona were credited with an interest too, but Benfica made it clear they would only consider selling Pavlidis if an irresistible offer arrived. His release clause is set at €100m (£86m).

The Red Devils will be hoping for a similar success story with Chido, who is viewed internally as a star of the future. The teenager made his United debut against Tottenham in February 2025 and has eight senior appearances to his name.

‌



He spent last season with the Under‑21s, scoring 15 goals in 31 matches, and has been a regular across multiple academy competitions - the EFL Trophy, National League Cup, FA Youth Cup, Premier League 2 and the International Under‑21s Cup.

United believe those fixtures have accelerated Obi's development and given him valuable experience ahead of his loan spell. The youngster arrived at Old Trafford in 2024 after spending four years in Arsenal's academy.

Sports.title: Eight players Man Utd could lose for NOTHING with urgent talks planned
Sports.content:
Eight players Man Utd could lose for NOTHING with urgent talks planned

Manchester United face the prospect of losing a chunk of their first-team squad with a host of them seeing their contracts expire in 2027 as the Red Devils consider who to invest in

View 2 Images Man Utd are ready to hand Bruno Fernandes a pay rise at Old Trafford

Manchester United have eight players who will see their contracts expire next summer - including Bruno Fernandes and Harry Maguire.

‌



Fernandes underlined his status as the club's talisman at the weekend as he scored a hat-trick in the win over Ipswich. His deal does include the option of a further year, tying him down until 2028, and the club have it on their radar to sit down with him sooner rather than later with financial rewards on the table.

‌



The Portuguese star is poised to become the club's highest earner as they prepare to bump up his pay from £300,000-a-week to £350,000-a-week.

‌



Other members of the squad, especially in the backline, will need to prove their worth over the coming season ahead of an overhaul. The defence is seen as the next area that needs addressing with the Old Trafford bosses ready to spend big - as they have done on midfield and attack in successive summers.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Luke Shaw, now 31, is out of contract next year and will likely need to take a cut on his £200,000 weekly salary if he wants to remain in Manchester, reports The Sun. Their pursuit of a new left-back was well documented, casting doubt over Shaw's future.

‌



At centre-half Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez are both men with contract sagas that are yet to play out. The Argentine has entered the final year of his deal but United are expected to trigger the one-year extension to keep him firmly tied down. Fitness has been an issue, but when available he's regularly been a strong performer.

Maguire meanwhile agreed a one-year contract with the option to stay for an extra 12 months in April. The 33-year-old is now the United vice-captain and has started in every game he has been available for under Michael Carrick, but ultimately age will eventually factor in. Especially with youngsters like Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven in the mix.

View 2 Images Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw will be watching on as the club prepare to bolster their defence

‌



A trio of young players in Harry Amass, Jack Fletcher and Tyler Fletcher will all see their contracts expire come the summer of 2027 and their futures may depend on whether they show enough to convince the United bosses that they have what it takes to cut it in the first-team.

Amass, who last year was on loan at Norwich and Sheffield Wednesday, is effectively Shaw's back-up this year but United were willing to offload him in the summer. The two Fletchers, who play in midfield roles, may see their routes into the first-team blocked off by the club's recruitment drive in that position, leaving them in an awkward predicament.

Veteran goalkeeper Tom Heaton will also be out of contract, having signed a new one-year deal to remain with the club in June. The 40-year-old is a hugely influential figure at Carrington and should he decide to hang up his gloves, he could stay at United in a different capacity.

Sports.title: Mo Salah jets back to Liverpool as wife gives birth to third child with name revealed
Sports.content:
Mo Salah jets back to Liverpool as wife gives birth to third child with name revealed

Mohamed Salah has found himself back in Liverpool, where his wife gave birth to their third child - and their first son - as his name was showcased on social media

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah and his wife have welcomed a third child (Image: Getty Images/Getty Images For The Premier League)

Mohamed Salah has flown back to the UK after his wife gave birth to their first son. The Liverpool icon left Merseyside in the summer after the two parties agreed to terminate his deal, but it was in the north west that his wife is reported to have given birth.

‌



Salah's sister Rabab has taken to social media to reveal that the couple had welcomed a son, who will be named Leil. The name translates to “night” in Arabic.

‌



The 34-year-old is now plying his trade in Turkey after opting to join Trabzonspor, and the club's president Ertugrul Dogan has revealed that Salah and another former Premier League star in Andre Onana have both seen their families grow.

‌



He said on 61saat: "After the (Amed SK) match, I travelled abroad with Salah and Andre Onana. Both of them had new children, Onana had twins and Salah a baby boy. I congratulate their families and their wives.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Magi is Salah's childhood sweetheart and they both grew up in their hometown of Nagrig. She later trained as a biotechnician with the pair marrying in 2013. Prior to their son arriving they had two daughters - Makka, their eldest, was born in 2014, and her sister Kayan arrived in 2020.

‌



Salah and his family had spent almost a decade in Liverpool and had planned to remain for another year but the two-year deal, which the Egyptian signed in 2025, was ripped up 12 months early. Salah though has stated the love he and his family have for the city.

He previously said: “They feel at home [here]. They were very happy, [wife] Magi and the kids, they were very happy that we're staying another two years. It feels like home so everyone was happy.”

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah's sister has revealed the name of their son

‌



Salah's time in Turkey has already seen the sudden departure of head coach Fatih Tekke from Trabzonspor, which follows the 5-0 aggregate defeat at the hands of Hungarian side Ferencvaros in the Europa League play-offs.

In light of that loss Salah said in a statement on social media: "Nothing in my career ever came easy. Bad nights and disappointments are part of football, and I have learned to turn them into motivation and into trophies. Trabzonspor is my club, and I am part of this project, body and soul. Last night will not change that. I know expectations are high, and I truly believe we can and will deliver. “I came here to win” is not just a slogan to me."

Sports.title: Inside Man City's window after £10m Enzo Fernandez discount and Ayyoub Bouaddi surprise
Sports.content:
Inside Man City's window after £10m Enzo Fernandez discount and Ayyoub Bouaddi surprise

Manchester City have transformed their squad during the summer window, with Enzo Maresca backed to the hilt as he faces the unenviable job of replacing Pep Guardiola

View 3 Images Manchester City believe they have completed a 'transformational' summer window

Manchester City bosses are said to be delighted with what has been described as a "brilliant" transfer window.

‌



Chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak and director of football Hugo Viana believe has given new manager Enzo Maresca a squad capable of winning back the league title from Arsenal. The final piece of the jigsaw came with the arrival of Enzo Fernandez in a deal costing City a joint British record £125m.

‌



But the process was kick started back in January, when Marc Guehi and Antoine Semenyo arrived at the Etihad ahead of schedule. Both had been targets for this summer, but City moved swiftly once it became known the duo were gettable six months sooner.

‌



Along with the arrival of Maresca to replace Pep Guardiola, the changes have been viewed as a "transformation", rather than a rebuild. And that the squad is much stronger now, compared to the start of what would become Guardiola's last season in charge.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Maresca is said to have high hopes for up and coming defender Vitor Reis, who is expected to have a breakthrough campaign.

‌



While teenage sensation Ayyoub Bouaddi is said to have made a huge impression in training since joining from Lille. Maresca is prepared to be patient with Bouaddi due to him being only 18, but will give him more games than people expect, due to his incredible talent.

City had been tracking him before the World Cup, but once he starred on the biggest stage of all in North America, the club decided to move quickly to get the deal done.

View 3 Images Ayyoub Bouaddi is already impressing Man City bosses (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Elliot Anderson has been signed to replace Bernardo Silva.

But the most significant deal of 2026 has been getting Fernandez. Maresca made it clear, having worked with him at Chelsea, City would be signing a proven winner at the high level.

Someone who can elevate midfield with his goals and assists, while bringing some much needed experience to a team lacking some of it in certain areas.

‌



At the start of the week the deal looked like it wouldn't happen. Chelsea were holding out for £135m and City were prepared to walk away.

View 3 Images City managed to get a deal over the line for Enzo Fernandez on deadline day (Image: Maja Hitij - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

But on deadline day the asking price dropped by £10m and City swooped. Negotiations were not concluded until within five hours of the window closing. City now feel the squad is built to challenge for trophies on all fronts.

Sports.title: Carlos Alcaraz planning more breaks in 'impossible' tennis schedule
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz has taken a swipe at the hectic tennis calendar and said he will skip tournaments from now on.

The Spaniard, who returned to action after ​a lengthy layoff due to a wrist injury sustained in April to defend his US Open title, said the demands of the schedule made ​it impossible for players to compete in every major ‌event without risking burnout.

The Spaniard pointed to the absences of other top stars as evidence that the schedule is too demanding and will keep causing injuries.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Carlos Alcaraz against Jaime Faria from the US Open

World No 1 Jannik Sinner and British star Jack Draper are notable absentees at Flushing Meadows along with Holger Rune, Joao Fonseca and a host of other players.

"I took more (time off) than I wanted, to be honest, but you know, seeing how tight the calendar is, obviously I don't want to have this break because (of) an injury," said Alcaraz after coming from a set down to beat Jaime Faria in the second round.

"But in the future, I'm going to take some breaks, some long breaks. Maybe not four months, but one month, two months, missing some tournaments, because it's impossible to play them all.

"I think they (are) adding more important tournaments. You know, in a way they (are) making us play. You can say 'no'. You can keep one or two.

"You can decide your calendar, but there are some Masters 1000s, some grand slams, and we've been out playing 40 weeks if we got to play every mandatory tournament that the ATP, you know, required us to play.

"So it's impossible, and we are seeing a lot of players getting injured, a lot of players getting tired. If they don't do anything about it, we are going to see even more in the future.

"But for me, taking this break because (of) an injury, it wasn't that good, but you know, what I'm going to say is I'm going to take some breaks and miss some tournaments in the future, for sure."

Sports.title: Osaka overcomes serving struggles to reach US Open third round
Sports.content:
Naomi Osaka overcame a mid-match wobble to beat Katerina Siniakova 6-2 5-7 6-1 and reach the third round of the US Open.

It wasn't quite as headline-grabbing a display - both on and off the court - from Osaka, who sported a more understated entrance outift, for which she is gaining increasing notoriety.

The two-time US Open champion had turned heads when wearing a long, white skirt and hooded robe featuring newspaper clippings about her ahead of her tournament opener on Monday night.

But on this occasion, Osaka opted for a more understated, shimmery all-white number which wouldn't have looked out of place at Wimbledon rather than Flushing Meadows.

Image: Naomi Osaka was taken to a deciding set before booking her place in US Open third round

The 13th seed was swiftly into her stride in the first set, breaking Siniakova to love in the fourth game of the opener, which she clinched with a second break of the Czech.

Osaka appeared to be cruising to victory in the second when breaking for 4-2 and 5-3 leads, only for her serve to desert her at that time as she was broken three times in a row to ultimately drop the set 7-5.

The four-time Gland Slam winner found her footing again for the decider, dropping only one game to clinch her spot in the next round.

Swiatek storms into third round in 71 minutes

Iga Swiatek also stormed into the third round of the US Open, with a clinical 6-3 6-2 win over Nadia Podoroska that took just 71 minutes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Iga Swiatek against Nadia Podoroska from the US Open

It was only the second meeting between the pair - the previous coming in the semi-finals of the 2020 French Open, with Swiatek victorious en route to claiming the first of her six Grand Slam titles.

The 2022 US Open champion, seeded eighth this year in New York, was back to her ruthless best.

She broke in the fourth game of the opening set and pushed on to take it 6-3, before snatching a crucial break of serve in the first game of the second set to ensure that she stayed firmly in control.

Podoroska showed some glimpses of her best form, but Swiatek was rarely under pressure and converted her first match point to book her place in the third round at Flushing Meadows for the seventh-straight time.

Sports.title: Penalised Antonelli to help Russell at Italian GP
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli is ready to help Mercedes team-mate and title rival George Russell in qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix for a race the world championship leader will start at the back of the grid due to an engine penalty.

Italy's own Antonelli arrives at his home track of Monza knowing that his healthy points advantage is almost certain to be eaten into this weekend owing to the fact Mercedes are triggering a back-of-the-grid start for him by exceeding power-unit component limits on his car, a legacy of reliability issues from earlier in the season.

Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton both trail Antonelli by 59 points while McLaren's Lando Norris, the winner of the last two races, is 83 points behind.

Given he already knows he will start at the back of the grid whatever result he achieves on Saturday, Antonelli is open to aiding Russell's qualifying session and bid for pole position by providing slipstream assistance to the sister Mercedes around F1's fastest track to provide a straight-line speed and lap-time boost.

"It has been discussed with the team," said Antonelli when asked about the tow in Thursday's Drivers' Press Conference.

"And, yes, we have agreed on a few things.

"So let's see, you know, how the session develops. But if the team will ask me to do so, I will do it. Because, yeah, obviously, I'm not fighting for... You know, of course, I will still be happy to do pole [by setting the fastest Q3 time], but, of course, I'm starting at the back.

"So, if I could do anything to help the team, I will do it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli says starting at the back of the grid in the Italian GP means he can 'enjoy' the race more.

Russell said the fact Antonelli was willing to help him out reflected well on Mercedes' culture.

The Briton is expected to take his own grid penalty for excessive engine usage at a later race, potentially at a similarly-overtaking-friendly Baku City Circuit in three weeks' time.

Russell said: "I think it just goes to show the level of teamwork we have at the moment between the two of us and how Toto [Wolff] wants to operate this team.

"I think that is a very good and unique opportunity for us, especially considering where we've both come from, being part of the [junior] programme from the very beginning. I think it's the least we should be doing.

"Last week [at Zandvoort] it worked well and if the roles were reversed, the same would have happened.

"This week he's willing to help me out in qualifying, which is great as well. That's just the way we are as a team.

"I will be taking a penalty at some point in the future. When and where I don't know."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Look back at some of the most dramatic moments to have taken place at the Italian Grand Prix.

But while Antonelli's penalty offers him a big chance to make up potentially significant title ground this weekend after falling 59 points behind at the Dutch Grand Prix, Russell stressed: "For me it doesn't change anything because I always want to focus on myself.

"Focus on my limitations and the areas I want to improve.

"I always said, it doesn't matter if I have a seven-time world champion as my team-mate, a rookie, or nobody, the job is still the same.

"So my approach will be exactly the same here this weekend."

'They are the team to beat right now' - Russell talks up McLaren but hopeful for Monza

While they continue to lead both world championship races, Mercedes' early-season dominance has been eroded in recent months with first Ferrari and now McLaren coming to the fore.

Russell is optimistic the high-speed Monza layout will be more favourable to their W17 than either of the last two races, which were won by McLaren, but expects all three of their chief rivals to remain big threats.

"As a team, we've won two races in the last six so we can say all we want but we'll soon find out," he said.

"I think there will be a lot of tough competition.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli says he understands the likely long-running speculation that Ferrari will make a move for him in the future, but insists he 'still has a lot to give back' at Mercedes.

"The momentum is with McLaren right now. Ferrari have upgrades this weekend. We know Red Bull have a very strong power unit. I honestly think this weekend it can be between any of the top four teams - but I hope it's us."

Russell, whose last Grand Prix win came in Austria at the end of June, added: "When you look at the past couple of races and how competitive Lando and McLaren have been, it's definitely very fair to say that they are the team to beat right now.

"We know we're an upgrade behind most and we hope we can go back to being the team to beat in a couple of races' time. But, for now, the fight [is] between McLaren and Ferrari, who have got the upgrades this weekend.

"I actually think we came away from Zandvoort having a very positive weekend as a team. I think a P2 and a P3 and a Sprint win was actually probably better than a true car performance."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix Sprint race.

And on Mercedes' chances of claiming a first Monza win since 2018, Russell said: "I don't know if we can say we're favourites this weekend but we definitely probably have a greater opportunity than we've had in the last two races where it's been less about the power unit and more about the chassis.

"As I said, I think we definitely have or had the best chassis and I think we will do again in the upcoming races.

"We can't forget Red Bull have a very strong power unit as well, we know this circuit is going to suit them more than the others. Ferrari with the upgrades. So I think it can be a four-team race this weekend."

Sports.title: Antonelli: Ferrari an incredible brand but I’m happy at Mercedes
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli played down suggestions that he could drive for Ferrari in the future as he claimed he could spend his entire career with Mercedes.

The 20-year-old Italian has exceeded all expectations to lead the Drivers' Championship by 59 points after 12 rounds of just his second season in Formula 1.

Antonelli's superb 2026 form has seen his popularity grow massively in Italy, creating a potential dilemma for the home fans at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix who would usually be loyal to Ferrari.

Asked about expectations that he could join Ferrari later in his career, Antonelli said: "Being an Italian myself, I know how emotional we are and how excited we can get about things. Sometimes overly excited.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli wins the Belgian Grand Prix.

"Of course, there will always be this kind of talk but, at the end of the day, as much as Ferrari is massive, incredible brand, I am very happy where I am.

"I am very happy with Mercedes because they are the ones who have given me the opportunity since I was a kid and I feel like I have so much to give back to them. Got to live with that."

Antonelli open to Verstappen-Red Bull longevity

Antonelli was later asked for his views on Max Verstappen's recent decision to sign a contract extension with Red Bull, who similarly signed the Dutchman as a teenager.

Verstappen was 17 when he was given a drive at Red Bull's then junior squad Toro Rosso in 2015, before promoted into the senior team during the following season.

The 2026 season is Verstappen's 10th full campaign with Red Bull, and Antonelli foresees a similar future for himself with Mercedes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico Rosberg discusses Max Verstappen's contract extension with Red Bull, saying it's a 'super important message' for the team.

"I think Max has an incredible relationship with Red Bull," Antonelli said. "Also, they were the one to put him in a car at a very young age. They were the one to put the trust.

"I feel like he's happy in the team, from what I can see. And he probably feels like wanting to stay with them. He probably believes as well in this project. So, I think he has all the reasons and all the rights to stay with Red Bull.

"And if one day he wants to change, then it's going to be up to him. But as long as he's happy where he is, why not?

"I will do the same with Mercedes is. I feel like I have, first of all, so much to give them. And if I will be happy all throughout with them, I will probably stay with them for my whole career as well.

"So, let's see. Of course, you never know what can happen."

'No real pressure' with grid penalty

Despite it being Antonelli's home race, Mercedes have chosen Monza as the circuit for Antonelli to receive a grid penalty for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.

Two separate engine problems earlier in the year made it inevitable Antonelli would have to take a penalty at some point, and Monza is viewed as one of the tracks where it's easiest to fight through the field from the back of the grid.

"In some ways it helps to release pressure, although I [would] very much rather fight for pole and start at the front," Antonelli said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli says starting at the back of the grid in the Italian GP means he can 'enjoy' the race more.

"But, in some ways, I feel like it makes me a bit more relaxed going into the weekend and that's why I am going to able to enjoy more the driving and the weekend itself.

"Of course, it's as well a different opportunity, an opportunity to try something different during the weekend. A different work method in free practice especially because we have the chance to do so.

"I think it's going to be a very interesting weekend."

Mercedes had previously explained that the decision had the potential to relieve pressure on Antonelli, both by decreasing expectations at his home event, and also by serving the penalty while he retains a significant lead at the top of the standings.

Antonelli leads both his Mercedes team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by 59 points, with McLaren's Lando Norris 83 points back in fourth after winning the last two races.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli goes past Mercedes teammate George Russell before retiring from the race with engine failure.

Antonelli added: "Of course, the goal is always the same and we're going to try and maximise the result.

"In an ideal world, I think realistically top five you can do well. But it's all driven also by your pace, how fast you are. What's the gap between cars? We might be really quick but Ferrari or McLaren or Red Bull they might be very close that it's not enough to catch them during the race.

"We'll see but I feel very free mentally going into this weekend. Very excited, very much looking forward to it, but with no real pressure."

Sports.title: Pakistan's cricket crisis: Have radical changes made side 'a laughing stock'?
Sports.content:
Nasser Hussain has criticised Pakistan's dramatic changes ahead of the final Test against England and feels the cricket board's decisions have made the team a "laughing stock."

Pakistan, 2-0 down after heavy defeats at Headingley and Lord's, have axed seven players for the finale at Edgbaston from September 9, including opener Imam-ul-Haq, wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan, spinner Ali Usman and seamer Khurram Shahzad.

Of the seven replacements, only two have played at Test level before in batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal.

Image: Sarfaraz Ahmed has been removed as Pakistan head coach with Mike Hesson in charge for the final Test at Edgbaston

Pakistan also removed head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul, with white-ball coach Mike Hesson in charge for the remainder of the tour.

'This is not not how to build a team'

Hussain, who spoke in frustration during Pakistan's 194-run loss at Lord's about how the tourists had faded as a force, said on the latest Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, as he and Michael Atherton were joined by Cricinfo senior editor Osman Samiuddin: "It is classic 'how you don't build a team' and fans deserve a little bit better.

"With the great teams, it's all about the greater purpose - whether that's Sir Viv Richards and Sir Clive Lloyd with West Indies bringing the islands together or the great Australia side playing for the baggy green cap under Steve Waugh.

"You create a side by making players feel wanted, so the ignominy of sending senior players home - okay, Rizwan has played a couple of bad shots, but he would give his heart and soul for Pakistan cricket.

"However well they go at Edgbaston, the players and coaches will know that the first time they fail that this may well happen to them.

Image: Pakistan wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan is another player to have been sent home

"The point of an administration is to alleviate pressure, not put more pressure on. I cannot see how an administration cannot see that. This may be a stroke of genius but it hasn't worked in the past, so why should it work now?"

How can a director of high performance 'throw a player under the bus'?

Aaqib Javed, the Pakistan Cricket Board's director of high performance, told a TV station in his homeland that drastic action had to be taken as "the world is laughing at us because we can't even compete".

Javed also launched an astonishing attack on Imam, saying the 30-year-old would face an inquiry after not batting in either innings at Lord's due to a calf issue.

He said to Geo: "The Imam injury is a big question mark, and a deep disappointment. Players in the past used to get injuries but used to put on casts and still tried [to play].

"We'll take action against this. How is it possible that a pulled muscle ruled you out of batting in both innings? He should have tried and fought. He'll have to face an inquiry. I can't say he faked it, but a muscle pull like that cannot stop you batting altogether."

Image: Imam faces an inquiry after he did not bat in either innings at Lord's

Hussain said: "I don't think after Headingley that the world was laughing at Pakistan.

"My rant at Lord's about them not fighting back, about India vs Pakistan games being very one-sided and that they were a poor side playing poorly wasn't laughing at them.

"It was out of frustration of seeing where this great cricketing nation is now. What they have done now is make them into a laughing stock. They have made it worse."

On the Imam situation, Hussain added: "I cannot believe how a director of high performance can go on telly, rightly or wrongly, and throw a player under the bus. He is either injured or he is not.

"For every other touring side, if we ask how a player is doing, they would say, 'he has had a scan and will only bat if needed'. The whole handling of the Iman situation is ridiculous. You have to protect your players a little bit."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the best of day four at Lord's as England thumped Pakistan by 194 runs to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match Test series

Atherton feels for Pakistan captain Babar

Asked by Hussain whether a win for Pakistan in Birmingham would justify such radical moves, Atherton said: "Not in this instance, no, because of the damage it will do longer term.

"This is no way to manage players and no way to build a long-term vision at all.

"I feel it's a horrible position for a captain, Babar Azam, to be in - and what kind of authority does he or indeed any captain of Pakistan have in this outfit?

"One understands that captain is not all powerful these days, you're not going back 30 years ago when they perhaps ran the show, but they have to have some authority within a team.

"Given what's happened, how do you lead that team now?"

Sports.title: Gabriel Martinelli leaves Arsenal for Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal in £60m deal
Sports.content:
Arsenal have confirmed Gabriel Martinelli has joined the Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal for £60m. It is understood the deal for Brazil forward includes a sell-on clause.

Martinelli, who joined Arsenal from Ituano in 2019, has fallen down the pecking order at the Emirates despite being part of the squad that won the Premier League title last season. His fee surpasses the previous record £40m received by Arsenal when they sold Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain to Liverpool in 2017.

Quick Guide How do I 

Martinelli is believed to have signed a four-year contract worth about £17m a season. His move was widely expected after Arsenal agreed a deal last week and has gone through before the transfer window in Saudi Arabia closes on Sunday.

The 25-year-old joins his Brazil teammate Gabriel Jesus in leaving Arsenal this week, the striker having moved to Barcelona for £8.6m. The Premier League champions also sold Fábio Vieira to Hamburg on deadline day but decided against bringing in players.

Arsenal are believed to have received about £3m from Brook Norton-Cuffy’s £14m move from Genoa to Hull owing to a sell-on clause in the England Under-21 defender’s contract but missed out on about £7m when Folarin Balogun move to Everton collapsed.

Tottenham have omitted Richarlison from their Premier League squad, with the striker not a part of their plans for the season. They could have accommodated him for the first-half of the campaign because one of their 17 senior non-homegrown players – Xavi Simons – is out until March or April, according to the manager, Roberto Di Zerbi, with an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Spurs made clear to Richarlison before the closure of the transfer window in England on Tuesday night that he would not be included so he could arrange a move. He was unable to do so, with one to his former club, Everton, not happening. He is the subject of firm interest from Trabzonspor in Turkey, where the window remains open until Friday night.

Richarlison posted a message on social media on Monday in which he said he would not allow anybody to decide his future for him. He talked about his commitment to Spurs; how “when everything here was falling apart and they needed me, I stayed and gave my life”.

Richarlison was Spurs’ top scorer in the league last season with 11 goals. He also said: “So I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I’ve always had for the Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

Sports.title: Mike Dean claims he played secret games for a laugh while refereeing matches
Sports.content:
The former Premier League referee Mike Dean claims he used to take part in secret challenges while officiating, including trying to stay in the centre circle for as long as possible, as he confessed to “just joking about” during matches. The remarks, made by one of the most well-known officials in the English game, have been met with bemusement by refereeing officials who say there is no evidence of any such behaviour having ever taken place.

Dean was a member of the select group of referees for more than two decades before he retired in 2022 and a brief spell as a video assistant referee followed. In an interview on Jamie Vardy’s podcast this week, Dean shared anecdotes from his time as a top-flight official in the pre-VAR era. “We used to say, ‘We’ll kick off now. Right, see how long we can go without blowing a whistle,’” he said. “I’ve done that a few times in the Premier League, before VAR obviously – [I] went 20, 25 minutes without blowing a whistle.

“I used to do another thing. I used to stand in the centre circle – see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about. I got about 15 minutes once.”

Officials within the refereeing organisation, Pro Ref, are understood to be puzzled by the claims, with the suggestion that a referee could stay in the centre circle for 15 minutes without someone noticing, for example, seen as highly improbable.

This is not the first time that Dean has courted controversy in a post-retirement interview. Dean was stood down from his role as a VAR in 2023 after failing to intervene over an error in a match between Tottenham and Chelsea, refereed by Anthony Taylor. Describing Taylor as a “mate”, Dean told Simon Jordan’s podcast that he had chosen not to ask Taylor to review his decision on a VAR monitor because he didn’t want him to have “any more grief than he already had”.

Dean earned notoriety during his time as a referee for his flamboyant mannerisms and apparent eye for the camera – as captured in the terrace chant “Mike Dean, it’s all about you”. But he was also held to be one of the best officials in the top flight, taking charge of 561 matches – and issuing a record 114 red cards – over the course of his 22-year career.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola defends transfer strategy and reveals Liverpool turned down options
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has defended Liverpool’s summer transfer strategy and said the club’s priority was to sign quality over quantity.

Liverpool had the highest net spend in the Premier League, with Bradley Barcola, signed for a potential £123m, added to a front line that includes the £125m Alexander Isak and £116m Florian Wirtz. Barcola could make his debut at Ipswich on Friday, despite not featuring for Paris Saint-Germain before his move on Monday.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Liverpool’s signings did not include a right back, defensive midfielder or right-winger but Iraola, who believes Barcola could be deployed in Mohamed Salah’s old position, insists the club’s approach was correct.

“I’m very happy with all the signings we’ve made,” said the Liverpool head coach. “I know the next question: ‘Do you want more signings in other positions?’ At the end the club has decided those signings we have done are the ones that improved our team and our position.

“There were other options we decided not to take, for different reasons: sometimes it is sporting reasons because they don’t improve what you have, sometimes it is economical reasons as it didn’t make sense in terms of the market to do those movements. But I’m happy now I know what we have, I have a lot of quality in the team and now it is the moment for us, for the players, for me to develop what we have.”

Despite the absence of a natural right-winger – Liverpool explored deals for Yankuba Minteh at Brighton and Ismaïla Sarr at Crystal Palace – Iraola is confident Barcola, Victor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Rio Ngumoha can provide sufficient cover.

He said: “I think we’ve preferred at the end to have the best players, probably, than a player that maybe is specifically for that [right-sided] position. I’m very used from my previous teams to demand for all the wingers to play both sides.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Probably all of them have played more on the left, but I would say I’ve seen them in a good place on the right. Probably Rio is more specific from the left side, but I think he has also showed the willingness to improve and play on the right. Even Bradley, he’s very open and I think he can play right and left. He started actually more on the right side when he started with Olympique Lyonnais. I’m happy with the four wingers we have and I’m sure we are going to be able to cover those two positions.”

Sports.title: World Cup wishlists, early movers, big clearouts: 2026 summer transfer window trends
Sports.content:
On the World Cup wishlist …

The World Cup is always a good shop window. Yan Diomande was already a rising star at RB Leipzig but shining for Côte d’Ivoire in the US helped push up his price tag before a £115.7m move to Real Madrid. There were other breakout stars: Switzerland’s Johan Manzambi, whose signature Aston Villa pipped Newcastle to; Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Kerim Alajbegovic, who went to Juventus; and Ghana’s Caleb Yirenkyi, who is now in the Premier League with Coventry. Cape Verde’s cult hero Vozinha now keeps net for the Chilean giants Colo-Colo and Morocco’s attacking dynamo, Ismael Saibari, has rocked up at Bayern. Billy Munday

Time is of the essence

While Europe’s wealthiest clubs generally allowed the World Cup to run its course before moving for their main targets, there were some exceptions. Real Madrid announced the signing of Marc Cucurella for £52m as he was getting ready to start Spain’s opener against Cape Verde, then Bernardo Silva before Portugal began their campaign two days later. Liverpool spent heavily early on as they signed Víctor Muñoz for £34.5m in mid-June and completed their pre-agreed £60m deal for Jérémy Jacquet at the start of July. Tottenham had spent almost £230m on Jan Paul van Hecke, Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali before the last 16 was over, also adding Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi on free transfers. Other clubs seemed to treat the World Cup as an opportunity to do deals under the radar. Bayer Leverkusen moved quickly, just as they did in January, to sign promising youngsters in Kennet Eichhorn and Afonso Moreira for a combined £32.8m in June. Brighton were among the most proactive squad builders in the Premier League, spending just over £50m on Zadok Yohanna, Costinha and Pascal Struijk before the World Cup action had moved beyond the last 32. Will Magee

View image in fullscreen Zadok Yohanna was an early arrival for Brighton, who did not wait around to make signings. Photograph: Toby Melville/Reuters

Premier League newcomers splash the cash

“Think about us like a volcano,” Hull’s owner, Acun Ilicali, said in July. “It’s boiling right now and it’s going to erupt.” He was not wrong. In the end, the promoted Premier League side signed 18 players this summer for a combined sum of £156.5m. Ipswich went even further, splashing £194.7m on 15 additions, while Coventry spent £122.4m on 11 new signings. It is a far cry from a few years ago when many promoted teams were frugal, often relying on the players who took them to the promised land. As recently as 2021 the three promoted teams, Norwich, Watford and Brentford, spent a combined £98.8m – with the latter’s acquisition of Kristoffer Ajer from Celtic the most expensive signing at £13m. The fact that Premier League newcomers are spending so lavishly is a reminder of the division’s financial dominance and the game’s increasingly extreme economic disparities. Marcus Christenson

French talent factory ups its output

In sharp contrast to the Premier League, where eight clubs had a net spend over £100m and only six made a net gain, 15 out of 18 Ligue 1 clubs made money on player trading this summer. Paris Saint-Germain led the way thanks in no small part to the £123m deal which took Bradley Barcola to Liverpool, making a net profit of more than £150m overall. Lille, who made around £100m, sanctioned big-money departures for Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo, who joined Manchester City and Newcastle for £85.7m and £51m respectively. Strasbourg, the smaller cog in BlueCo’s transfer machine, brought in almost £90m as they moved on Diego Moreira, Julio Enciso, Abdoul Ouattara, Guéla Doué, Valentín Barco and Emmanuel Emegha – the latter two moving to, that’s right, Chelsea. While Ligue 1 has been a conveyor belt of talent for some time, its output is reaching new levels. Of the 15 biggest fees ever received by French clubs, five have come in this window. WM

View image in fullscreen Bradley Barcola was the most expensive of numerous acquisitions from Ligue 1 clubs. Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty Images

Fiorentina lead clubs in clearout mode

There has been plenty of upheaval this summer, but nowhere more so than at Fiorentina. After battling relegation for much of last season, eventually finishing 15th in Serie A, the Viola have moved on 34 players either permanently or on loan, with Moise Kean and Tariq Lamptey among the high-profile departees. No other club in Europe’s “big five” leagues can match that but Chelsea, with 33 leavers (18 on loan), are not far off. While Chelsea made a net profit of around £60m thanks to the £125m deadline-day deal for Enzo Fernández, Fiorentina have spent more than £100m net on a rebuild from the ground up. Depending on interpretation, that’s either a sign of Premier League money taking on a bizarre and irrational life of its own, or a lesson in the eye-watering cost of fixing a failed recruitment strategy. WM

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Inter order the full English

There has been a steady stream of English players heading to Italy in recent years, but it’s not often three turn up at one club in quick succession. Inter have opened the floodgates this summer, signing John Stones from Manchester City on a free, Djed Spence from Tottenham for £25.6m and Curtis Jones from Liverpool for £25.7m. The pantheon of Inter cult heroes includes Paul Ince and Ashley Young, who won the Scudetto in 2021, so the club has a longstanding Anglophile streak, but Serie A has also become an increasingly attractive destination. With Omari Hutchinson joining Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek at Milan, the derby will have a distinctly English flavour. WM

View image in fullscreen Curtis Jones savours victory against Cagliari on his Inter debut. Photograph: Mattia Pistoia/Inter/Getty Images

It is Ireland v Scotland in the frontlines of Seville this season. Perhaps inspired by their pre-season trip to Dublin, Real Betis spent £17.1m to sign Troy Parrott from AZ, where he scored 31 goals in the Netherlands last season. Manuel Pellegrini said moving to La Liga is a “leap” for Parrott, but it’s not as big a jump as Robbie Ure has made. The £5.6m Glasgow-born striker, uncapped by Scotland, has become Sevilla’s new No 9 off the back of 15 goals in 15 games in the first half of the Swedish season for the unlikely Allsvenskan leaders, Sirius. “I wanted to be in top-class environments,” the 22-year-old said. BM

Transfer tumbleweed and tight pockets

They may have been the least active club in Europe’s top leagues this summer with zero new arrivals but, given their tradition of only signing players born or trained in the Basque Country, Athletic Bilbao have a good excuse. Marseille, not so much. Other than fulfilling their pre-agreed obligations to buy Timothy Weah and Hamed Traorè, OM have not brought in a single player while stripping their squad back to the bare bones in a drastic attempt to repair their finances. Then there are the clubs with modest budgets who have opted for a thrifty approach. Málaga, newly promoted to La Liga, have brought in seven players but not paid a single transfer fee. Le Mans, new arrivals in Ligue 1, have limited themselves to two undisclosed fees while making nine signings, also allowing five players to leave without receiving a fee in return. WM

Sports.title: Manchester City’s Vivianne Miedema could miss rest of year with knee injury
Sports.content:
Manchester City could be without Vivianne Miedema for at least the rest of 2026, the Guardian understands, after the Netherlands forward sustained a knee injury.

According to multiple sources the injury is not an anterior cruciate ligament but is serious and there are fears she will not return until after the Women’s Super League’s winter break. A statement from the club on Tuesday said Miedema would miss the “start of the season”.

City are understood to have sought reinforcements in attacking midfield to cover for Miedema, who predominantly played as a No 10 for the WSL champions last term. The Paris Saint-Germain and Nigeria midfielder Jennifer Echegini and the Everton and Spain forward Ornella Vignola are players City are understood to have inquired about before the 11pm BST WSL transfer deadline. According to sources, PSG are not willing to sell Echegini.

Arsenal are expected to finalise the signing of the France defender Élisa De Almeida from PSG . The club are understood to have agreed a fee of just over £500,000 for the 28-year-old.

De Almeida, who played for PSG since 2021, is an experienced centre-back and was part of France’s Euro 2025 and 2023 World Cup squads. Arsenal are understood to need centre-back cover partly because their defender Katie Reid’s recovery from the anterior cruciate ligament injury sustained last November is being managed carefully, meaning the 19-year-old is not expected to be available before November.

The summer window has been another record-breaking one for the women’s game globally. The latest mid-year snapshot report released by Fifa on Thursday showed global spending on international women’s transfer fees this summer had surpassed $28m (£20.7m), more than double last summer’s $12.3m. In 2022 it was $1.23m. English clubs led the spending this summer with $8m, followed by Spain ($6.6m) and Germany ($4.9m).

The promoted side Crystal Palace made a deadline-day signing with the return of Shanade Hopcroft. The 28-year-old former Chelsea academy player, who helped Palace win promotion in 2023-24, has signed a two-year deal.

The WSL season gets under way on Friday when London City Lionesses host Manchester United. The new United head coach, Eva Olid, said on Thursday her team would not add more signings. United secured the Mexico midfielder Rebeca Bernal, who can also play at centre-back, on Wednesday, and Olid said at her first press conference since replacing Marc Skinner that Bernal would be available for Friday’s match.

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s head coach, Eva Olid, said: ‘It was not about signing players quick. It is about signing the right players.’ Photograph: Poppy Townson/MUFC/Manchester United/Getty Images

Olid, the former Hearts manager, is promising to bring “attacking football” to United. She used the word “attacking” eight times during her 17-minute press conference and spoke of her enthusiasm for developing young players. She said of her attacking style: “They appointed me for that reason. I have to go with that. We will be brave in attack, trying to play that attractive football. Our main focus [is] that attacking mentality. We want to play with the ball, a nice football, create a lot of chances.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

On waiting until January before adding more players, Olid said: “The players I need are different from the players the previous manager needed. [It has been a] short period to react. We have some plans in January about signing players that I really need for my style of play. It was not about signing players quick. It is about signing the right players.”

Olid was also asked about United’s investment in the women’s game, with Chelsea spending nearly three times as much as them on their women’s team wage bill in the most recent set of published accounts. Olid spoke positively about her club’s backing, saying: “The message has always been about: ‘We want to invest in everything.’ As I said, not just on players. Because I think it is important we have the right staff, the right coaches … The message is that they want to win. They want to win. I think I am here to make that happen, but with a solid identity.”

Arturo Ruiz, who was appointed as Brighton’s head coach on 28 August, acknowledged at his first press conference that he had not had much time with his players but said: “We need to be patient and put the focus on high-performance, and results will come. If that [happens] soon, it’s better, but if not, we need to be very clear in our gameplans.”

The 29-year-old former Real Sociedad head coach added: “Our style of play will be very adaptable without the ball, very aggressive when we need to [be], very compact when we need to be as well, and defending the box really well. With the ball, we are going to be a very dynamic team with a clear identity.” Brighton host Arsenal on Sunday.

Sports.title: The WSL returns bigger than ever and with a mouthwatering title race
Sports.content:
It has been a summer of change for women’s football in England, with expansion of the Women’s Super League to 14 teams bringing three new sides into the fold, huge transfers hitting the headlines, changes to the League Cup and a new name on the WSL trophy as we prepare for kick-off on Friday.

Players have had a proper break over the summer, with no major international women’s tournament for the first time in six years (Covid delays pushed back the Tokyo Olympics to 2021 and the European Championship to 2022, followed by the 2023 World Cup, 2024 Paris Olympics and Euro 2025). As a result, managers have had a full pre-season with all available players for the first time in more than half a decade too.

In many respects, this is the most mouthwatering and unpredictable WSL season of recent years. At the top end, the title race is wide open from the outset. The holders, Manchester City, have perhaps the most settled squad and a potent attack spearheaded by the winner of three back-to-back Golden Boots, Bunny Shaw. However, they will also be juggling their league and FA Cup title defences alongside Champions League football, which they avoided last season through a fourth-place finish in the league the preceding year. That will be counteracted somewhat by Champions League teams no longer competing in the rebranded League Cup, which also opens the door to domestic silverware for those outside the top three.

Arsenal and Renée Slegers have no excuses for a poor season, after two disappointing and costly starts to WSL campaigns were somewhat understandable due to the tight turnarounds following the major tournament exploits of many players and Champions League qualifying campaigns in the 2022-23 and 2023-24 season. The Gunners have overhauled their squad in the summer and lowered the age profile, adding experienced top-level talent such as Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle, Géraldine Reuteler and Selina Cerci.

Chelsea have embarked on their own squad evolution, after a transitional season where they sought to strike the balance between making changes and retaining that winning spirit synonymous with the side. Some hugely influential and longstanding players have departed in Millie Bright, who has retired, Guro Reiten, Sam Kerr, Catarina Macario, Johanna Rytting Kaneryd and Niamh Charles.

Melvine Malard, who has reunited with Sonia Bompastor having played under her at OL Lyonnes, has already hit the ground running with two goals from the bench in the team’s 5-2 win against Real Sociedad in the first leg of their Champions League qualifier. Where playing in Champions League qualifiers was a burden in seasons after major international tournaments, this campaign it could be an advantage for the Blues who have a chance to shake off any rust before they kick off their title challenge.

It perhaps feels a little unfair to drop Manchester United out of the title challengers and to place them in with “the best of the rest” but, with a nine-point gap between them and Chelsea last season, a lack of serious backing from the club and a so far underwhelming transfer window, this season could be a tough one for them.

Marc Skinner’s exit after a frustrating five years in Manchester was welcomed by sections of their fanbase but the manager arguably helped the side to punch well above their weight, with a comparatively small wage bill despite a competitive turnover. Eva Olid is an exciting young manager, having led Hearts from the bottom of the Scottish Women’s Premier League (with the team avoiding relegation only because of league expansion) to the title before her departure at the end of last season. However, if fans are hoping for a fresh start they should perhaps temper their excitement, with the club leaning into Olid’s reputation for player development and their four summer recruits so far not doing anywhere near enough to offset the loss of their outgoing players.

View image in fullscreen Eva Olid talks to the media on the eve of the new WSL season. Photograph: Poppy Townson/MUFC/Manchester United/Getty Images

They could be troubled by a chasing pack who have invested shrewdly, in the case of Tottenham, Everton, Liverpool and Brighton, or boldly, in the case of London City Lionesses.

United’s first challenge is against Michele Kang’s big-spending side as they open the WSL season on Friday night, when the two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas will answer the question of whether she can “do it on a Friday night in Bromley”.

The London City manager, Eder Maestre, has the enviable job of being able to put together his dream team, but the unenviable task of trying to gel a side that have had 13 departures and eight players coming in. The decision to remove the manager that led them into the WSL, Jocelyn Prêcheur, was billed as a purely football one by sources, with the club sixth in the table in their first season in the top flight. That decision, though, shows Kang will not accept mediocrity and the patience required by Maestre may not be forthcoming.

Tottenham and Brighton are two other teams aiming high. Martin Ho’s Spurs are the league’s not-so-dark dark horses, with a hugely impressive debut season for their manager followed by an astute and targeted transfer window, which has included the recruitment of the third-highest scorer in the league last season, the midfielder Kirsty Hanson, and the club-record signing Alice Sombath from OL Lyonnes.

The impact of the shock departure of Dario Vidosic from Brighton, with his move to the NWSL side Angel City announced soon after, will be fully known when the season gets under way, but they have recruited a very promising young replacement, Arturo Ruiz, and their squad has huge potential after a strong window.

Everton, Liverpool and West Ham all have potential to be surprise packages this season after similarly impressive transfer windows as the middle to lower end of the table ups its game.

View image in fullscreen Everton will be looking to make an impact in the top half this season. Photograph: Tony Smith/Alamy

Aston Villa have recruited 10 to replace the nine departed players but the fear will be that the incoming players struggle to fill the hole left by players such as Hanson, Ebony Salmon and Gabi Nunes.

Of the newcomers to the WSL, Birmingham and Crystal Palace have overseen similarly large squad turnovers, with some top-level talent brought in to attempt to ensure they avoid the drop back down to WSL 2 such as Millie Turner and Lisa Naalsund for the former and Bethany England for the latter.

Charlton have not been able to recruit so ambitiously in the summer, though eight new players have arrived to help the manager, Karen Hills, and her side who hope to leave egg on the faces of many who have put them as favourites to go down.

Predicting results or the outcome of the season is nigh- on impossible though, and that will be the hope: that the expanded league delivers surprises.
