Sports.title: Loan stars: Premier League youngsters to watch in the EFL
Sports.content:
Ollie Whatmuff, Manchester City to Stockport

Goalkeepers are supposed to peak at about 30, which makes one wonder how good the 18-year-old Whatmuff will be at that point. He spent last season playing professionally, earning promotion from the National League with Rochdale under the tutelage of Jimmy McNulty. When the manager jumped two divisions to Stockport, Whatmuff was the first person he wanted to take with him. City showed how highly they think of Whatmuff by incorporating him within their pre-season tour travelling party, where he worked closely with Gianluigi Donnarumma. Whatmuff is extremely composed with the ball at his feet, unfazed by pressure and his surroundings. Those who have worked with him are confident he will spend his career in the Premier League and win full international honours.

Samuel Iling-Junior, Aston Villa to Bolton

The winger has spent his career flitting between England and Italy, taking in Juventus, Middlesbrough, West Brom and Pisa along the way. It feels like a fascinating career but one that needs a more permanent setting. Wingers who can use both feet are incredibly desirable and Iling-Junior is further aided by his pace. Wherever he has been, the 22-year-old has never made his mark consistently but he has the qualities to succeed and requires more game time to hone the skills that enabled him to score in Serie A and earn 16 England Under-21 caps.

View image in fullscreen Bolton’s Samuel Iling-Junior takes on Sheffield United’s Romelle Donovan (left) and Rhys Norrington-Davies (right). Photograph: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock

Charlie Gray, Manchester City to Wigan

Pep Guardiola gave the midfielder his City debut, a fine reward for someone who joined aged five and is an FA Youth Cup winner. He made steady progress until 15 when he sustained a fractured spine, then showed admirable courage and desire to return, only to fracture his shins. The holding midfielder, described as “clever and intelligent” by Guardiola, is regarded as happy to sit in front of the defence. This season was viewed as the right time for Gray to progress his development in the third tier. Gray was not used by Gary Caldwell in Wigan’s opening three games, all of which were lost, but started Wednesday’s home victory against MK Dons.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Mason Melia, Tottenham to Lincoln

It cost a League of Ireland record for Tottenham to sign the forward, who made almost 100 first-team appearances for St Patrick’s Athletic before leaving as an 18-year-old in January. Clubs from across the pyramid and around Europe were interested in Melia, whose clever movement is a key part of his game. He is able to play as the focal point of the attack but can also drop deep and get on the ball. A natural finisher, he will be pushing for more chances at Lincoln, who managed one shot on goal from 18 attempts in their goalless draw with Blackburn on Tuesday.

View image in fullscreen Mason Melia is unveiled at Lincoln. Photograph: Chris Vaughan/Getty Images

Lamin Sillah, Nottingham Forest to Gillingham

The striker, spotted in the Gambia playing for Steve Biko FC, has ticked off time with Olympiakos and Forest. It will be interesting to see how the speedy forward adapts at a club that have scored twice in their opening four matches. Silleh’s ceiling is above the fourth tier but he needs some polishing and that begins with facing League Two defenders on a weekly basis, learning the tricks of the trade from gnarled centre-backs who do not take kindly to Premier League kids.

Tommi O’Reilly, Aston Villa to Doncaster

This is a fifth loan for the midfielder, whose journey has taken in the Basque County and Crewe with a few stops in between. It was at Gresty Road last season that he found his feet, playing every game in League Two and scoring seven goals. During his academy days, teammates would compare him to Phil Foden thanks to his skill and style. Grant McCann spent a long time developing young talent at Peterborough and is doing the same at Doncaster, where O’Reilly is aiming to keep his career on an upward trajectory.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Keyrol Figueroa, Liverpool to Port Vale

It would be great to come up with plenty of reasons to follow the striker’s progress from in-depth scouting to being tipped the wink by a Liverpool coach but, ultimately, everyone just wants to see how the son of the former Wigan full-back Maynor Figueroa gets on in League Two. Maynor was a cult hero at the Latics and is still turning out for Whythenshawe Vets. Keyrol spent his youth career playing for USA, the country of his birth, but earned his first Honduras cap this year. He will need a further 180 to match his dad.

Rio Cardines, Crystal Palace to Bristol City

The full-back’s first two Palace games were against Dynamo Kyiv and Arsenal and he has 11 Trinidad & Tobago caps but this season his ability will be consistently challenged. The early signs are good for an athletic, speedy defender eager to get up and down. Versatility made him an attractive option for the Robins, where Michael Skubala is using Cardines at left-back despite the 20-year-old spending more of his career on the right. The change is working because Cardines has made three assists.

View image in fullscreen Rio Cardines of Bristol City (right) in action against Patrick Roberts of Birmingham. Photograph: Ryan Crockett/PA

Harry Howell, Brighton to Leicester

Howell’s selection for a Premier League bench at 16 shows what Brighton think of the attacking midfielder but he had to wait until he turned 17 for his debut against the then champions Liverpool. A cultured player who rolls down his socks, Howell can play in numerous roles in the final third. He was awarded a three-year deal before being sent to Leicester to join the Russell Martin evolution, which includes two more Brighton loanees, Tommy Watson and Kamari Doyle. Howell’s father, Jamie, was a professional who started his career at Arsenal and his cousin Jack Hinshelwood has become a Brighton regular.

Sports.title: Hull condemn ‘disgusting’ racist abuse of deadline-day signing Robinio Vaz
Sports.content:
Hull City have condemned racist ⁠abuse directed at their new signing Robinio Vaz on ⁠social media ⁠and ​said they were working with authorities to identify ⁠those responsible.

The 19-year-old striker joined the promoted ⁠Premier League side on loan ​from Roma ‌on transfer deadline day. Vaz’s move was announced in a social media post that garnered a high volume of derogatory comments aimed at the Frenchman.

“No individual ‌should ever experience discriminatory abuse, and the club will provide Robinio with our full support,” Hull said. “We ‌are also working with Humberside police and other relevant ​authorities to identify the accounts responsible for this disgusting abuse, so that appropriate action can be ⁠taken against those individuals.”

Quick Guide How do I 

The Premier League said it strongly condemned the abuse and had offered its support to Vaz and the club. “We are disgusted by the ongoing discrimination players face on social media and are committed to working with clubs, authorities, law enforcement and social media companies to address this issue,” it said.

Hull have enjoyed ​a ​strong start to ​life back in the ​top ‌flight, winning ​their ​opening two matches, and host Aston Villa on Saturday.

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley locked out of West Ham ownership as Daniel Kretinsky becomes majority shareholder
Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley locked out of West Ham ownership as Daniel Kretinsky becomes majority shareholder

David Kretinsky has agreed a deal with the Gold family to become West Ham's majority shareholder, talkSPORT understands.

As such, Amanda Staveley, who helped lead the Saudi-backed 2024 takeover of Newcastle, has effectively been blocked from buying a stake in the Hammers.

2 Kretinsky is now the Hammers' majority shareholder Credit: Getty

talkSPORT also understands David Sullivan has increased his ownership of the club to 40 per cent.

Following the death of co-chairman David Gold in 2023, his daughter Vanessa took control of a 25.1 per cent share in the club.

Kretinsky's fresh investment

Czech businessman Kretinsky first invested in West Ham back in 2021.

His stake is now set to increase beyond the 38.8 per cent held by Sullivan.

talkSPORT reported last month that Kretinsky had reduced his stake from 27 per cent to below 25 per cent in an effort to prevent Staveley from investing.

The billionaire is believed to have sold part of his share to fellow Czech Jakub Havrlant.

A consortium led by Staveley had been eyeing up the Gold family's stake, worth around £150m.

Sullivan was forced to step down as West Ham chairman in June after accusations of sexual abuse were made against him.

The 77-year-old, who made much of his fortune in the adult entertainment industry, has vehemently denied the claims.

West Ham get their season up and running

This latest development in the Hammers' ownership saga comes amid the beginning of their mission to make an immediate return to the Premier League following relegation last season.

Nuno Espirito Santo's side picked up their first win of the Championship campaign on Tuesday, beating Wolves 4-2 at the London Stadium.

2 Nuno's West Ham got their first league victory of 2026/27 at the fourth time of asking Credit: Getty

Divine Mukasa bagged a brace for the hosts, with Jarrod Bowen and Konstantinos Mavropanos also on the scoresheet.

The result, which came after fans had chanted at their previous game for Nuno to be sacked, took West Ham into the top half of table, a point off the play-offs at this early stage of the season.

Next up for the Hammers is another home game against Derby on Saturday.

West Ham dropped back into the second tier after 14 years in the Premier League, their longest top-flight stint since the 1970s.

Their last Championship stint lasted just one season as they were promoted via the play-offs in 2011/12.

Sports.title: How to watch Cristiano Ronaldo’s next match as Ange Postecoglou bids to continue perfect start
Sports.content:
How to watch Cristiano Ronaldo’s next match as Ange Postecoglou bids to continue perfect start

Cristiano Ronaldo's Al-Nassr will be aiming to make it five Saudi Pro League wins from five under Ange Postecoglou on Saturday.

Al-Nassr have made the perfect start to their title defence and sit second behind league leaders Al-Hilal only on goal difference.



2 Postecoglou boasts a 100% record in charge of Al-Nassr so far Credit: Getty

Former Tottenham boss Postecoglou succeeded Jorge Jesus as head coach this summer and has overseen five wins in all competitions, with Al-Nassr also beating Al-Diriyah in the King's Cup.

And his side are back in action away to Al-Ittihad this Saturday (September 5) at 7pm BST.

How can I watch Ronaldo's next match?

You can stream Al-Ittihad vs Al-Nassr live on talkSPORT.com.

For a small fee, you'll be able to stream every available Saudi Pro League game.



Ronaldo's season so far and what's next

Ronaldo scored his second goal of the campaign as Al-Nassr came from behind to beat Al-Taawoun 2-1 last time out.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner has made three Saudi Pro League appearances so far this term as he continues to captain the club – though he didn't take kindly to being substituted in the recent 3-2 win over Al-Ettifaq.



However, he has admitted the 2026/27 season is likely to be his last.

The 41-year-old, who has one year left on his contract at the Riyadh-based club, told Vogue last month an interview about his wedding to Georgina Rodriguez: "This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy.

"I have my future all mapped out. I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard. Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one.



"Have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really like, and continue to enjoy what I've earned – what we've earned.

2 Ronaldo has scored well over 100 goals for Al-Nassr Credit: Getty

"Because after all it's been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice."

Ronaldo joined Al-Nassr in 2023 following the end of his second spell with Manchester United.

He's racked up 131 goals in 151 appearances in all competitions so far, averaging almost a goal a game in the Saudi Pro League.



He won the division's Golden Boot in 2023/24 and 2024/25.

Who else can I watch in action for Al-Nassr?

Ronaldo is among a number of former Premier League stars currently plying their trade for Al-Nassr.

He's joined by fellow Portugal international and ex-Chelsea man Joao Felix, as well as Premier League-winning Liverpool great Sadio Mane.

Sports.title: Everton consider bringing Jamie Vardy back to Premier League aged 39
Sports.content:
Everton are reportedly weighing up a shock move for Jamie Vardy after missing out on Folarin Balogun.

The Toffees tried to sign Balogun from Monaco on deadline day, but the deal for the USA striker collapsed.



2 Vardy spent last season in Italy with Cremonese Credit: Getty

Everton's frantic search for a striker

They also had a late loan approach for Joshua Zirkzee rejected by Manchester United.

But talkSPORT understands Everton have been offered the chance to sign former Man United striker Anthony Martial on a free transfer after he left Mexican side Monterrey earlier this year.

With the Toffees selling Beto to Fiorentina, they find themselves badly short at centre-forward.



Thierno Barry is now their only senior out-and-out option in that department.

But that figure could rise to two if Everton complete the signing of Vardy, with The Sun reporting the veteran is firmly on the Toffees' radar.



Vardy is available

Vardy is currently a free agent after leaving Cremonese at the end of his contract this summer.

The 39-year-old Premier League legend scored seven goals in his one and only season with the Serie A side, who he was unable to save from relegation.



Vardy had joined Cremonese after his glittering 13-year stay with Leicester to an end in the summer of 2025.

The former England international racked up 200 goals for the club, famously firing them to a fairy-tale Premier League title in the 2015/16 campaign.

He also helped the Foxes to 2020/21 FA Cup glory and to two promotions to the top flight either side of their unforgettable title triumph.

2 Vardy won the prestigious FWA Footballer of the Year award for his part in Leicester's Premier League success Credit: Getty



Winner of the Premier League Golden Boot in 2019/20, Vardy turns 40 in January but doesn't seem to have any plans to retire just yet.

Cremonese were the fifth club of his long career that began with South Yorkshire eighth-tier outfit Stocksbridge Park Steels back in 2006.

Famously a late bloomer, not making his top-flight debut until the age of 27, Vardy continued his rise through non-League with FC Halifax Town and Fleetwood Town before Leicester came calling in 2012.

The Foxes paid a then English fifth-tier record £1m to secure his services.



That record stood until just last week, when Swedish club Djurgardens signed winger Abdul Abdulmalik for an initial £1.5m from National League Boreham Wood.

An all-time Premier League great

Vardy scored 145 Premier League goals for Leicester, placing him 14th on the competition's all-time list.

He struck 20 or more times in three separate top-flight seasons, peaking with 24 goals en route to the title in 2015/16.

Capped 26 times by England, he notched seven goals for his country, including one in the win over Wales at Euro 2016.

Sports.title: Abbi Summers: Chelsea got karma and Arsenal fans will reluctantly agree with me on obvious mistake
Sports.content:
Abbi Summers: Chelsea got karma and Arsenal fans will reluctantly agree with me on obvious mistake

Chelsea's failed move for Lamine Camara was karma for offloading Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhailo Mudryk to Tottenham Hotspur.

That is according to talkSPORT's Abbi Summers, who also believes Premier League champions Arsenal have made a key mistake.



4 Chelsea's failed move for Camara was karma for offloading players to Spurs, says Summers Credit: Getty

Summers has reviewed the summer transfer business of several clubs following deadline day earlier this week.

The Premier League window slammed shut with teams spending a record £3.41billion combined.

'Spurs signed unwanted players'

Spurs contributed over £300million to that figure after a glut of signings were made to bolster Roberto De Zerbi's squad.



They included late deals for Chelsea duo Tosin and Mudryk, with the latter arriving on a season-long loan, with a £75million option to buy.

Their moves came after Manchester City had hijacked Spurs' attempt to sign Iliman Ndiaye from Everton.



Giving her judgement on the double signing, Summers admitted: "We went from Iliman Ndiaye to signing Tosin and Mudryk.

"That was not on my bingo card. That was not on anybody’s bingo card if I’m totally honest with you. We never do business with Chelsea, we haven’t I think since (Carlo) Cudicini.



"If you’re going to do business with Chelsea, please make it be a good player, but it just seems to me like we have taken two players that, I mean it’s well-documented, they didn’t want, couldn’t get rid of.

"Have offered Tosin out to god knows who and we’ve just been like ‘yes, ok sure, we’ll have them, no problem.’"

Tosin had been offered to clubs in the Premier League and overseas by Chelsea this summer.

4 Mudryk followed Tosin in joining Spurs from Chelsea on deadline day Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



The centre-back was also left out of the squad for each of their opening three matches of the season.

As for Mudryk, the Ukraine international was only cleared to return to action this summer after his doping case was resolved.

The 25-year-old, who previously played under De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk, had been provisionally suspended since December 2024.

Prior to the ban, Mudryk scored 10 goals and added 11 assists in 73 appearances for Chelsea.



Camara deal 'karma' for Chelsea

According to Summers, the Blues have already been dealt some Karma for shifting their unwanted stars to London rivals Spurs.

Xabi Alonso missed out on the deadline day signing of Camara after Monaco pulled out of a £47million deal at the 11th hour.

As a result, Chelsea were unable to secure a replacement for Enzo Fernandez, who was sold to City for £125million.

Despite that, Summers was impressed by their attacking signings earlier in the window, with Morgan Rogers added to the frontline.



She explained: "Chelsea had a phenomenal window. Their front line is scary.

"When you think Cole Palmer is bang in form, Joao Pedro looking great and then you’ve added Morgan Rogers to the mix. They are looking unreal. They really are.

"(Maxence) Lacroix, good signing. (Emi) Martinez, they had to sort the keeper situation out, good signing.

"The only thing I would say is losing Enzo Fernandez and not getting Camara over the line.



4 Summers believes Chelsea have had a 'phenomenal' window after bolstering their attack Credit: Getty

"I mean, I think that’s banter. It’s jokes because you’ve just lumbered Spurs with Tosin and Mudryk, so a tiny bit of karma there and who doesn’t want to see Chelsea suffer a little bit?

"But considering how injury-prone their midfielders are and the people that can also cover in midfield as well, you’re leaving yourself in a bit of a tricky situation.

"I know that the Chelsea fan base were losing their minds over the fact that they couldn’t get that deal done in time and it collapsed in the final hour.



"Have they done enough to be title challengers? I think everyone was saying with the window they’ve had, Chelsea are really dangerous, which they are going forward.

"But we’ve seen in the first few games so far that they definitely have weaknesses at the back and are just leaving yourselves in a really vulnerable position not signing a replacement for Enzo Fernandez."

Although Chelsea have made a winning start to the season, they have conceded five goals across their victories over Fulham and Brighton.

Meanwhile, Moises Caicedo has already picked up a knock, joining summer signings Jordan Henderson and Marco Palestra on the treatment table.



Arsenal's transfer mistake

Whilst Summers admits Chelsea have a 'phenomenal' attack, she has concerns over Arsenal's forward options.

She believes even the most reluctant of Gunners fans will agree they made a mistake not signing another attacker.

Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Leandro Trossard were all allowed to leave the club after last season's title triumph.

However, the exciting addition of Christos Tzolis proved to be their only signing in attack.



Elsewhere, Arsenal have also signed the likes of Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes.

4 Tzolis was the only forward player signed by Arsenal this summer Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Turning her attention to Mikel Arteta's side, Summers added: "I think Arsenal’s business has been very good.

"I think bringing in Ezri Konsa, that’s a great signing. They love a centre-back as well. This is where centre-backs go to thrive and develop. It’s literally their kingdom.



"Bruno Guimaraes, great signing too. Tzolis has looked positive as well in the first couple games that we’ve seen. He literally looks like a baby Trossard.

"But I do think that by selling Martinelli, letting Gabriel Jesus go and of course letting Trossard go, they have left themselves extremely light in those attacking areas.

"Of course, you have got versatility. You can play (Eberechi) Eze on the wing, you have (Noni) Madueke that can also play on both wings, (Kai) Havertz, (Viktor) Gyokeres, fine.

"But I think that if Arsenal fans were being honest, they would definitely say they are probably a little bit underwhelmed by that area of the pitch in this window.



Arsenal's 2026 summer transfer window In: Bruno Guimaraes (Newcastle United) - £75m

Ezri Konsa (Aston Villa) - £55m

Piero Hincapie (Bayer Leverkusen) - £45m

Christos Tzolis (Club Brugge) - £34m

Illan Meslier (Leeds United) - Free Out: Leandro Trossard (Besiktas) - £18m

Jakub Kiwior (Porto) - £15m

Gabriel Jesus (Barcelona) - £8.6m

Fabio Vieira (Hamburg) - Undisclosed

Christian Norgaard (Everton) - £7m

Karl Hein (Werder Bremen) - £2.6m

Reiss Nelson (Feyenoord) - Free

Ethan Nwaneri (Borussia Dortmund) - Loan

Tommy Setford (Stevenage) - Loan

"The rest has been good, but selling three players and only bringing in one in Tzolis, that could be a bit risky."

Martinelli's impending exit to Al Hilal will leave Tzolis as Arsenal's only recognised left winger.

Meanwhile, Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz are their only senior centre-forwards.

Arteta is boosted, though, by the ability of his other forwards to play in a multitude of attacking roles.



Arsenal have a 100 per cent record after two matches this season, beating Coventry City and Aston Villa.

Ahead of Sunday's visit from Chelsea, they only trail league leaders City on goals scored.

Sports.title: Two Arsenal players missing from training days before huge Chelsea showdown
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes and Cristhian Mosquera both missed Arsenal training three days before Sunday's home London derby against Chelsea.

Arsenal had an open training session on Thursday morning, but Guimaraes and Mosquera were not involved.



2 Guimaraes played his first 19 Premier League minutes for Arsenal last time out Credit: Getty

Good news and bad news for Arsenal

Both players featured in Monday's 1-0 win at Aston Villa, with Guimaraes making his Premier League debut for the Gunners from the bench following a short spell on the sidelines.

Mosquera started the game but was forced off towards the end of the second half by a muscular problem.

It remains to be seen whether either will be available for the visit of Chelsea, where both sides put their 100 per cent starts to the season on the line.



Guimaraes had started last month's Community Shield victory over Manchester City but missed Arsenal's Premier League opener against Coventry with a minor groin issue.

The Brazil midfielder was Arsenal's most expensive signing of the summer transfer window, joining from Newcastle for £75m.



Mosquera had been covering for the injured William Saliba, though the Gunners have also signed Ezri Konsa – who replaced Mosquera for the final 10 minutes against Villa, the club he'd just arrived from.

Konsa could be in line to make his first Arsenal start this weekend, then.



Saliba is expected to be out until at least the middle of October with a back injury.

More positively on the injury front for Mikel Arteta, Declan Rice has been training after hobbling off late on in the Villa game.

Jurrien Timber has also been back training solo after missing the Netherlands' World Cup campaign through a groin injury.

2 Mosquera has started all three games in all competitions for the Gunners this term Credit: Getty



The Gunners' perfect start

Arsenal have begun their Premier League title defence in ideal fashion, kicking off by beating Coventry 3-0 before picking up three more points and keeping another clean sheet last time out.

But Chelsea are set to present their sternest test of the campaign so far.

Xabi Alonso's Blues are the joint top-scoring side in the Premier League so far with seven goals – and while they've also conceded six goals themselves, they have successfully seen off Fulham 3-2 and Brighton 4-3.

Arsenal, though, have an excellent recent record at the Emirates Stadium against their London rivals.



Chelsea haven't won there since August 2021, with the Gunners coming out on top in each of the last five meetings in all competitions in north London.

Chelsea team news

The Blues have a number of injury worries of their own: Jordan Henderson remains sidelined after breaking his arm in a freak incident at the World Cup, while fellow summer signing Marco Palestra – also yet to make his debut – is still doubtful.

Alonso will also be hoping the issue that forced Moises Caicedo off against Brighton is not serious, as he initially thought.

Sports.title: Nine big-name players out of contract next summer from Harry Kane to Bruno Fernandes and two Liverpool stars
Sports.content:
Nine big-name players out of contract next summer from Harry Kane to Bruno Fernandes and two Liverpool stars

The summer transfer window may have just closed, but that does not stop the rumour mill churning.

One of the big talking points at the end of every season is the high-profile names who are out of contract and therefore have freedom of choice over their next destination.

9 Silva joined Real Madrid this summer in a blockbuster free transfer Credit: Getty

This summer we have seen the likes of Bernardo Silva join Real Madrid and John Stones head to Inter Milan. Meanwhile, people like Jadon Sancho are still without a club.

Those who are available in July 2027 for nothing will already be on the radar of clubs around Europe and beyond.

From January, those players can enter negotiations with clubs outside their current league and sign pre-contract agreements, should they wish to.

And there are some superstars who, currently, have their contracts expiring next summer.

talkSPORT.com has taken a look at the nine biggest names with less than a year left on their deals.

Harry Kane

The England captain is, as things stand, going to become a free agent next summer.

If this were to come to pass then it would create pandemonium around Europe. He is arguably the best player in the world right now and a favourite for the Ballon d’Or.

In all likelihood, the 33-year-old will sign a new contract extension with Bayern Munich, talks have started.

But if those break down then it could put plenty of teams on high alert. One sticking point appears to be the length of the deal.

Kane said: "The first meeting was this week. But such matters are not settled in a week or two. There will be many other discussions about the details."

9 Kane has scored 148 goals in 150 games for Bayern Credit: Getty

Asked about the contract clauses, the England captain added: "I won't talk about the details here."

Things are going well, so everything is fine so far. We will continue the dialogue in the coming weeks and see what happens."

Kane added: "There are many factors that affect a contract like this: I am 33 years old, so this may not be my last contract, but it is certainly an important contract for me. I need to be happy, and the club also needs to be happy.

“The good thing is that both parties are not worried. At the moment, they are just open discussions, as is the case with any contract in my career."

Bruno Fernandes

Fernandes remains Manchester United’s best player and has been for some time.

The 31-year-old is at the peak of his powers and showed that with a hat-trick against Ipswich on Sunday.

9 Fernandes is the reigning PFA Player of the Year Credit: Getty

United were prepared to sell him last summer when Al Nassr came in with an £80m bid. Ruben Amorim was said to have blocked his exit.

The Red Devils are keen to get Fernandes to sign a contract extension to make him the best paid player at the club.

He currently earns around £300,000-a-week, but that could increase by another £50,000.

The reigning PFA Player of the Year has also been named Manchester United’s best player in five of his seven seasons at the club.

Lisandro Martinez

World Cup winner Martinez is facing a fight to save his Manchester United career.

As reported in the talkSPORT Notebook, sources have confirmed the club are ready to take up the extra year’s option in Martinez’s contract, which is due to expire at the end of the season.

9 Martinez joined Man United from Ajax in 2022 Credit: Getty

However, there is a feeling inside the corridors of power at Carrington that the Argentine needs to prove his ability to stay fit or be sold next summer.

Since joining United from Ajax four years ago, Martinez - affectionately known as ‘The Butcher’ by fans - has missed almost 80 Premier League games due to various injuries. He also turns 29 in January.

If United decide against activating that extra year option, however unlikely, then the 28-year-old would be free to walk away.

Christian Pulisic

USMNT star Pulisic is entering the final 12 months of his contract with AC Milan, who do still hold an option of extending that for another year.

Reports emerged earlier this summer that Major League Soccer (MLS) club New York City FC were looking to make a move for the forward, offering a salary of $11.3 million per season over a five-year contract.

AC Milan were not entertaining the idea of selling him this summer, but his future is sure to be a hot topic of discussion come July.

9 Pulisic left Chelsea in 2023 for AC Milan Credit: Getty

Brahim Diaz

The 27-year-old is now in the final 12 months of his contract at Real Madrid.

There has long been talk over negotiations to extend his deal until 2030, but as yet there has been no sign of an official announcement.

Should these talks break down or not happen, then he would be available on a free transfer next summer.

The Morocco World Cup star has started one game this season for Madrid, but will find increasing competition for a place following the signing of Yan Diomande.

9 Diaz started his career at Man City before joining Real Madrid in 2019 Credit: Getty

Alisson

Liverpool triggered Alisson Becker’s one-year contract extension last season to keep him at the club until 2027.

The likelihood is the 33-year-old will leave Anfield after an illustrious nine seasons, where he has won two Premier League titles and the Champions League.

Liverpool already have Giorgi Mamardashvili as his back-up and recently signed 18-year-old Lucca Brughmans from Genk, where he has returned on loan for the 2026/27 campaign.

9 Alisson has played 335 games for Liverpool Credit: Getty

Virgil van Dijk

Van Dijk is another Liverpool stalwart expected to end his time at Anfield at the end of the season.

He penned a two-year extension in April 2025, taking him until the summer of 2027.

There are no signs that it will be increased further for the 35-year-old club captain.

Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni are expected to be his long-term replacements.

9 Van Dijk was worth every penny of the £75m Liverpool paid Southampton in 2018 Credit: Getty

Kaoru Mitoma

The 29-year-old has been a revelation in the Premier League since joining Brighton from Kawasaki Frontale in 2021.

The Japan star was denied a trip to the World Cup this summer after suffering a hamstring injury during a Premier League game in May.

His contract will expire at the end of the season, with the dynamic winger expected to be hugely in demand should he be available on a free transfer.

Tyrick Mitchell

Mitchell has been the model of consistency at Crystal Palace over a number of seasons, flourishing under Oliver Glasner.

He helped Palace win the FA Cup, Community Shield, and Conference League.

The 27-year-old has perhaps been unlucky to be constantly overlooked for a place in the England squad.

The Palace academy graduate has played 246 times since making his debut in the 2019/20 campaign.

There will likely be plenty of interest should he not extend his stay at Selhurst Park beyond the end of the season.

Sports.title: Sunderland star in talks over late transfer exit amid Europa League squad snub
Sports.content:
Chemsdine Talbi has been left out of Sunderland's Europa League squad as talks continue over a potential move.

The Black Cats have submitted their 22-man squad for the continental competition following a hectic summer.



2 Talbi is likely to leave Sunderland in the coming days Credit: Getty

The 21-year-old has featured sporadically for the north-east outfit, and was benched in the 1-0 win over Fulham last weekend.

talkSPORT understands the Morocco international has been in talks with Saudi Pro League club Al-Ittihad.

Turkish Super Lig clubs Galatasaray and Fenerbahce are also interested in the winger.



Because the transfer windows in Saudi Arabia and Turkey remain open, Talbi can still seal a move away from Wearside despite the Premier League deadline having passed.

The youngster only signed for the club from Club Brugges for £18million last summer.



Speaking in a press conference on Thursday, Sunderland manager Regis Le Bris said: "A move remains possible so it's important to respect both parties. We'll see.

"He's still a good player, huge potential but after that you still have a window to decide if it's the right pathway here.



"I believe he can succeed here, but after that it's a question of mutual confidence and you have to respect the player's choice."

Who is in Sunderland's Europa League squad?

Robin Roefs and Simon Moore are the named goalkeepers in the Europa League squad.

The nine defenders are Omar Alderete, Dan Ballard, Kevin Danso, Trai Hume, Reinildo, Dayann Méthalie, Thomas Meunier, Nordi Mukiele and Luke O'Nien.

2 Talbi became a crucial player at times for Sunderland last season Credit: AFP



Midfield options are Jules Ahoka, Habib Diarra, Enzo Le Fee, Chris Rigg, Noah Sadiki and Granit Xhaka.

The forwards are Nilson Angulo, Brian Brobbey, Malick Fofana, Wilson Isidor and Romaine Mundle.

Eligible youngsters can still be registered on List B during the league phase; but Talbi does not meet those requirements.

He is young enough to meet the age requirement for List B, but he cannot be registered through that route because he has not been at Sunderland for the required two-year period.



The Morocco international netted four times in 28 Premier League games during his first season in the English top-flight.

After the campaign, Talbi was selected in Morocco's 26-man squad for the World Cup in North America.

Sports.title: Mike Dean criticised after viral clip admitting to ‘playing games’ while refereeing
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League referee Mike Dean has been criticised for admitting he played 'mini-games' while officiating.

Dean became arguably the most recognised official in English football after taking charge of 553 top-flight matches over a 22-year career.

2 Dean retired as a video assistant referee (VAR) official in 2023. Credit: Getty

He was often labelled by fans as 'arrogant' and made a name for himself as one of the biggest personalities in refereeing.

The 58-year-old hung up his whistle following the 2021/22 campaign and became a VAR official.

Since retiring from the game completely, Dean has launched a media career, offering his insights on the game as a former referee.

He recently went viral during an appearance on Jamie Vardy's new podcast.

Dean said: "There used to be games that we used to have, as a laugh, we used to say, 'Right, we'll kick off now, right? See how long we can go without blowing a whistle.

"Done that a few times in the Premier League, before VAR obviously. Went 20–25 minutes without blowing the whistle a few times. Let it go, let it go, let it go.

"I used to do another thing in the Premier League. I used to stand in the centre circle and see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about.

"I used to do another thing in the Premier League. I used to stand in the centre circle and see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about."

It has sparked a backlash among fans, with ProRef deciding to make no comment when approached.

talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor, who played for Aston Villa during Dean's career, was left furious by the revelation.

2 Dean was at the centre of many huge Premier League moments during his career Credit: Getty

He said: "I didn't get on with Mike Dean at all. He's the sort of referee that gives it back to players.

"He had that arrogance about him. One word to describe him. I would say he's a prat. That's just the perfect word for him.

"I just think back to games now and I'm like, you were refereeing games and you were having a joke about.

"It’s like, ‘Oh okay, I want to beat my friend who I've had a little joke with. How long can we go without blowing our whistle or leaving the centre circle?,

"Referees should be up and down so they don't miss anything, there was no VAR back then.

"So you might have missed penalties or free kicks because you want to joke and stay in the centre circle."

It is not the first time that Dean has prompted controversy when speaking about his career.

The ex-official has previously admitted not referring a decision to VAR, in an attempt to protect a friend.

During a fiery draw between Chelsea and Tottenham in August 2022 and claimed he avoided sending Anthony Taylor to the screen to review a missed hair pull on Marc Cucurella as his colleague had endured a tough match.

Sports.title: Sunderland winger Chemsdine Talbi is left out of their Europa League squad - just a year after joining for £18m
Sports.content:
Sunderland winger Chemsdine Talbi is left out of their Europa League squad - just a year after joining for £18m

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Al Ittihad are in talks with Sunderland over a move for winger Chemsdine Talbi.

The Moroccan international is free to move to the Saudi Pro League now as their window is still open.

Talbi has not been named in Sunderland's European squad due to him being subject of talks with Al Ittihad.

The 21-year-old winger joined Sunderland from Club Brugge for £18million last summer, and made 30 appearances last season. He came off the bench in their opening game of this campaign, a 2-1 defeat at Ipswich.

Manager Regis Le Bris says he is happy with this summer's transfer business after their trio of deadline-day signings.

The Black Cats made six additions over the window in preparation to compete on domestic and European fronts, with Le Bris suggesting the club managed to tick three boxes.

Al Ittihad are in talks to sign Sunderland winger Chemsdine Talbi, with the Saudi Pro League transfer window still open

They had a busy final day of the window before signing winger Malick Fofana from Lyon for £30m. Crystal Palace attempted to hijack the move and the deal was in limbo before Sunderland convinced him to join. They also landed Kevin Danso from Spurs and 18-year-old Ecuadorian centre forward Juan Riquelme Angulo from Independiente del Valle.

'We had this mantra at the beginning of the market – keep the core, add what we need. We kept this idea all the way,' the Sunderland boss said.

'It was tough obviously because the market is not easy to manage. We ticked our three boxes, the first one with Kevin Danso and Thomas Meunier – top level experience.

'The second one with Malick and Dayann (Methalie) – young with proven experience. The third one is the huge potential prospects with Juan (Riquelme Angulo) and Jules (Ahoka). We had to manage the different positions, because it's already a big challenge, but at the end we are happy.'

Meunier, Methalie and Ahoka had all joined earlier in the summer before Sunderland bolstered their squad with three further signings on the final day of the window as Danso, Fofana and Angulo all arrived.

Le Bris added: '(Angulo) will fill this third striker position. It's important to match the demand of this position, you have to be an underdog and be patient but also with the potential to play because it's important across the different competitions we'll have.

'Kevin, he has authority, physicality, leadership, he's a great player and in this position at centre back it's important to have this experience and this composure.

'For Malick, wingers are a specific role; so good in one v one, strong personality to go again, even if it's difficult to manage duels. He combines well, is committed defensively. He's an exciting profile.'

Sports.title: Richarlison AXED from Tottenham's Premier League squad by Roberto De Zerbi: Wantaway star left out as he pushes to join Mo Salah in Turkey after Everton transfer saga and cryptic social media messages
Sports.content:
Tottenham have axed Richarlison from their Premier League squad but a proposed move to Trabzonspor has yet to be completed.

The Brazilian international forward, who has one year remaining on his Spurs contract with the option for another year, is a transfer target for the Turkish Super Lig club who shocked football earlier this summer by signing Mohamed Salah on a free transfer.

Turkey's transfer deadline is on Friday, and Richarlison is understood to be keen to make the move to link up with Salah and Fabinho, another former Liverpool favourite and a former Brazil team-mate.

Spurs however have yet to receive a bid they consider acceptable. They valued the 29-year-old at £35million in a deal set up with Everton for £65m Iliman Ndiaye last weekend.

Richarlison was told in advance of Tuesday's transfer deadline that he was not part of Roberto De Zerbi's plans for this season and could leave for the right price.

After omitting him from the squad beaten by Newcastle on Saturday, De Zerbi said the former Watford and Everton striker signed for £60m in 2022 had asked to leave 'too many times'.

Richarlison has been axed from Tottenham's Premier League squad as he seeks a move to Turkey

Roberto De Zerbi said on Saturday the former Watford and Everton striker had asked 'too many times' to leave

When Spurs confirmed their Premier League squad on Thursday, there was a place for Xavi Simons despite a serious knee injury which is expected to rule him out until next year, and for Dejan Kulusevski who has not played for 19 months since a serious knee operation but is back in training.

There is also a place for Wilson Odobert, also out with a serious knee injury, is also included although now classifies as a homegrown player.

Richarlison issued cryptic messages on his social media channels earlier this week as the possibility of a return to Everton emerged as part of a trade with Ndiaye, who ended up signing for Manchester City on deadline day.

The Brazilian posted a picture on Instagram of a slogan saying: 'I am the villain of many poorly told stories.'

He then added: 'If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I'll return to my beloved club. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy. But the negotiations weren't going the way people wanted, and it won't be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I'll be available to the club'

Only after the English transfer deadline passed did the possibility of a move to Trabzonspor emerge.

Reports from Turkey claimed personal terms had been agreed with the player and that bids had been made, although Spurs rejected any such bids had been received.

By leaving him out of the squad, the pressure is back on Trabzonspor to strike a deal with Spurs.

Sports.title: Arsenal sell Gabriel Martinelli: Brazilian becomes club-record sale after completing £60m move to Saudi side Al-Hilal
Sports.content:
Gabriel Martinelli has joined Al Hilal in a club-record £60million sale for Arsenal. The deal, which is a fixed fee and includes a sell-on clause, surpasses the £40m Arsenal sold Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain for to Liverpool in the summer of 2017. He has signed a four-year deal and will wear the No 7. Martinelli's move to the Saudi Pro League comes after fellow left-sided forward Leandro Trossard was sold to Besiktas. Although the Gunners signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge, the departures of both Martinelli and Trossard - who scored a combined 19 goals for the club last year - opens Arsenal up to being exposed in that area of the pitch. Eberechi Eze will feature more as a left-sided forward this season while the belief at the club is that both Noni Madueke and Bukayo Saka can also operate on that flank, too. Gabriel Martinelli has joined Al-Hilal on a four-year deal from Arsenal after a £60million move Martinelli's exit is a club-record sale for Arsenal - breaking Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's record Martinelli, who has played nearly 300 times for the Gunners across seven seasons, was left out of Arsenal's squad for their Community Shield win against Manchester City and subsequent Premier League victories over Coventry and Aston Villa. Former Arsenal striker Ian Wright said the treatment of Martinelli left him feeling 'uncomfortable' and claimed the 25-year-old deserved 'more respect'. While the Premier League transfer window closed on Tuesday, the deadline for the Saudi Pro League is on Sunday.
